member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.ArchiveDiskCache
member.summary:
F-M370: archives kept on disk between runs, keyed by .
The run cache (F-M369) only helps inside one run — but a season pack serves one episode per run, and with the free daily limit at 50 downloads a season needs several days. Measured on 01.11.2026: 51 archive fetches for 45 files, 26 of them on three packs; the run stopped at 98 of 1300 queued items because the quota was gone, so the next run asks for the same packs again. Every avoided fetch on disk is one more file per day.
Two switches, both in the Download tab: days (0 = off) and megabytes (0 = off). Either at 0 disables the whole thing. The ceiling is enforced oldest-first, and only .zip bodies under are stored, so a runaway upstream cannot fill the volume.

member.name: F:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.ArchiveDiskCache.MaxEntryBytes
member.summary: Ceiling per archive: bodies above this are not written (F-M386: own constant, it used to be borrowed from the removed run cache).

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.ArchiveDiskCache.PurgeDirectory(System.String)
member.summary:
F-M427 (operator order 03.11.2026: "Cache bei db reset bitte mit purgen"): removes every archive this cache wrote, and nothing else.
Static and folder-based on purpose: a reset must be able to purge without a live instance, and the directory is the plugin's own (`<data folder>/archive-cache`), so no path is passed in from a caller that might get it wrong. Leftovers under .tmp go with it — an interrupted store leaves one behind.
member.returns: Number of archives removed.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.ArchiveKey
member.summary:
F-M370: the part of a download URL that names the ARCHIVE, not the entry inside it.
SubDL hands out one URL per archive entry, so a season pack that serves nine episodes arrives as nine different URLs that share nothing but their first path segment — measured on 31.10.2026: Xhfe8mD1w5/5Ibw144l42, Xhfe8mD1w5/SUK5YnspZX, … for one pack, 0p9xSnSU4g/… nine times, BlwZSYtLaU/… seven times. Keying a cache on the full URL therefore never hits, and the same pack is downloaded ten times in one run.
The key comes from the URL alone — it is known before anything is fetched, so a cache can answer without a request. Only characters that are safe as a file name pass; anything else yields null and is simply not cached, rather than cached under a key that mixes two archives.

member.summary: Builds the cache key for a download URL.
member.param: Absolute download URL, with or without query string.
member.returns: The archive segment, or null when the URL carries no usable one.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.ArchiveKey.IsCacheable(System.String)
member.summary: Whether the URL can be cached at all, so the client can decide before it asks a cache a question the cache cannot answer.
member.returns: Whether a key exists.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.DownloadOutcome
member.summary:
The verdict of ONE download attempt: the status, the byte count and the error name of that attempt, together with the body it produced. Every fetch returns one of these, so no consumer reads state that a later call may already have overwritten.
Measured 11.11.2026, why this type exists: the client carried the verdict in three mutable properties that every attempt overwrote. Four separate defects came out of that one shape — a reject quoting the previous candidate's 200 (F-M456), a route that recorded nothing at all (F-M461), a finding that died because a later candidate succeeded (F-M462), and an empty answer that was believed twice (F-M455). The verdict belongs to the call that produced it.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.Endpoints.Provenance
member.summary:
F-M486/F-M487 (operator order 15.11.2026: "Kreuzkontamination bitte verhindern — ein Download von tvst soll nicht bei subdl hochgeladen werden und umgekehrt"): the provenance of a subtitle — which source it came from — and the one rule that keeps the two sources apart.
The store carries the provenance per subtitle (Origin, OriginId, schema 10). It is the only place the fact survives: the file on disk says nothing about where it came from, and a content hash names the TEXT, not its origin.

member.summary: The value written for SubDL.

member.summary: The value written for tvsubtitles.net.

member.summary: F-M486: the store value for a source.
member.returns: The value the store keeps.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.Endpoints.Provenance.Parse(System.String)
member.summary: F-M486: the source a stored value names, or null when the row does not say.
member.returns: The source, or null.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.Endpoints.Provenance.MayUploadTo(System.String,Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.SubtitleProvider)
member.summary:
F-M487: may this subtitle go to that source?
UNKNOWN provenance is allowed everywhere — a hand copy, an embedded track or an older row says nothing about where it came from, and refusing those would stop the plugin from uploading the operator's own files. A KNOWN provenance is allowed at its own source only: a subtitle fetched from tvsubtitles.net never becomes a SubDL upload, and a SubDL download never goes back out to tvsubtitles.net. That is the whole rule, and it is deliberately this short.
member.param: The source that would take the upload.
member.returns: True when the upload may go there.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.Endpoints.Provenance.CrossSourceReason(System.String,Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.SubtitleProvider)
member.summary: F-M487: the sentence a refused cross-source upload is logged with — the same wording in the log and in the store's reason, so a looked-up row explains itself.
member.returns: The reason line.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.GlobalRateLimiter
member.summary:
The pacing rhythm shared by the upload AND the download pipeline (F-M20/F-M26).
It owns NO budget. An earlier build kept a per-run hourly call bucket here and let it stop a run — a limit the plugin had invented itself and then obeyed. SubDL publishes only DAILY counters, so the bucket stopped runs the server would have allowed; it is removed (03.10.2026, user decision). What remains is the spacing between calls and the plus/minus 30 % jitter on real transfers (anti-thundering-herd, F-M26).
Nothing in this class can refuse a call. Thread-safe across both pipelines.

Deterministic: the explicit when configured, otherwise the interval derived from the transfer rate (3600/rate). This pause carries NO jitter — the jitter belongs to the transfer rhythm ().
member.returns: Delay in milliseconds.

member.returns: Delay in milliseconds.

member.name: F:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.GlobalRateLimiter._fitMsPending
member.summary: F-M310: milliseconds of audio alignment not yet credited against the transfer rhythm. Written on the thread that measured a fit, read at the next pause.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.GlobalRateLimiter.AddFitMs(System.Int64)
member.summary: F-M310: books the duration of one audio alignment. The alignment runs AFTER a subtitle was downloaded and BEFORE the next real download, so it sits inside a transfer pause that was sized for a download only — the rhythm was charging the run for time it spent correcting, not transferring. Nothing is banked: the credit can only bring the NEXT pause down.
member.param: Measured milliseconds. Zero and negative values are ignored.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.GlobalRateLimiter.TransferPauseMsLessFit
member.summary: F-M310: the pause before a real transfer, less the alignment time booked since the last one. Floor 0: the plugin never waits a negative time, and an alignment longer than the pause simply means no further wait. The credit is CONSUMED here — taking it twice would shrink two pauses for one alignment.
member.returns: Delay in milliseconds, never below zero.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.GlobalRateLimiter.PauseAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Waits one bare-call pause. This is the whole throttle now — it cannot fail, because there is no bucket left to run dry (F-M20).
member.returns: A task that completes after the pause.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.JsonFields
member.summary:
Readers for the fields SubDL sends.
These exist because the same field is not always JSON-typed the same way across endpoints. Measured live (28.09.2026, 37 search hits across 4 queries): hi and full_season arrive as JSON booleans, while the numeric fields (season, episode, framerate) arrive as numbers. A reader that insists on ONE kind silently yields the default for every other kind, and because the default of a flag is "off", the failure looks like "the feature does nothing" rather than like an error. That is exactly how hi was lost: it was read with an int-only reader, so every candidate came back as "not hearing impaired".
The rule for this plugin: read what the API actually sends, accept the documented alternates, and keep ONE implementation here instead of a copy per class.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.JsonFields.GetBool(System.Text.Json.JsonElement,System.String)
member.summary: Reads a flag. Accepts the JSON booleans as well as the 0/1 form some endpoints use, because the same logical flag is not uniformly typed across SubDL's endpoints.
member.returns: The flag, or false when the property is absent or unusable.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.JsonFields.ToBool(System.Text.Json.JsonElement)
member.summary: Converts one JSON value to a flag: booleans as sent, numbers by "non-zero", strings by the usual literals ("true"/"false", "1"/"0"). Anything else is false rather than an exception — a missing flag must never abort a download run.
member.returns: The flag.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.JsonFields.GetDouble(System.Text.Json.JsonElement,System.String)
member.summary: Reads a number that the API may send as a JSON number OR as a numeric string. Live example: fps comes as the string "23.976" on some entries and is absent on others, so an int-only reader silently returned "unknown" for every value that was actually present.
member.returns: The number, or 0 when absent or unusable.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.QuotaStopDecision
member.summary:
F-M238 (user decision 28.09.2026): the decision after a 429, as a rule apart from the code that acts on it.
It sits here — pure, with no config, no clock and no coordinator — because the expensive mistakes are all in this one branch: a spent allowance that stops without scheduling anything never retries until the next regular anchor, and an unknown allowance read optimistically becomes a retry storm against a limit that may already be reached. Both are answerable from four booleans, so both are asserted directly.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.QuotaStopDecision.Decide(System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Decides the retry shape.
An allowance that is SPENT and one that could not be READ take the same path: the day-long one. The pipeline cannot tell "no quota left" from "quota unknown", and of the two possible mistakes only one is recoverable within the hour — treating an unknown allowance as available spends requests against a limit that may be reached.
member.param: The direction's "Continue after daily limit" setting.
True when an arrival event started this run.
True when the counter for this direction is spent.
True when the counters could not be read or carry no limit.
member.returns: The retry shape for this direction.

members.member:
In-run watchdog (NF-4): aborts a pipeline run when no heartbeat has been recorded for a fixed grace period of .
The grace used to be scaled from the configured rate limit (2.4–3.8 min). That was wrong in both directions: it could abort a legal transfer — one file download is allowed 5 minutes (FileTransferTimeout), a value the scaled grace never reached — and it tied a robustness limit to a pacing setting. With the local call budget removed (F-M20) there is nothing left to scale from, so the grace is a constant that covers the longest legal single operation with room to spare.
The heartbeat keeps the watchdog quiet while the run is making progress.
F-M209: torn down on EVERY exit path, so a run that leaves on an exception leaves no timer and no subscription behind.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.RunWorkFiles
member.summary:
F-M441 (operator 04.11.2026, "kein dauerhafter store"): the working files of ONE run.
The pack fill used to hold the text of every subtitle track of every file it touched in a dictionary for the whole run — measured on prod 04.11.2026 that was 689 episode files, roughly 21.000 texts and an estimated 900 MB resident. The texts now live on disk while the run works and are gone when it ends: a second pack asking for the same episode reads the file instead of calling ffmpeg again, and nothing survives the run.
Nothing here is a source of truth. A missing file is simply a re-extraction; the directory is purged at the end of the run and any directory left behind by a killed run is swept at the start of the next one.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.SeasonEpisodeIndex
member.summary:
F-M372: how many episodes a season HAS — asked at IMDb, TMDB as the fallback.
A season pack claims to SubDL that the season is complete (is_full_season=true). That claim is about the season that AIRED, not about the folder on disk: eight of ten episodes is a complete folder and an incomplete season. The library can therefore not answer the question — it only knows what it holds.
IMDb's own GraphQL endpoint answers it per season. Two details matter: every episode carries series.episodeNumber, and episode 0 is a real entry (Game of Thrones S01 reports 11 episodes: ten plus the unaired original pilot at E0), so the aired set is the distinct numbers above zero.

member.param: TMDB series id, used for the fallback.
TMDB API key, empty when TMDB is not configured.
member.returns: Aired episode numbers, or null.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.SubdlAdoptController
member.summary:
F-M423 (operator order 02.11.2026): adopts uploads this account already published before the plugin knew about them into the registry.
The problem it solves: a season only becomes a pack when EVERY episode carries the language as an uploaded row. Rows are only written by this plugin, so everything an earlier seeder published is invisible — on 02.11.2026 the registry held no row at all for 23 of 23 Person of Interest S1 episodes while SubDL carried fourteen English singles for them, and For All Mankind S1..S5 (10 of 10 episodes each) produced no pack for the same reason. The uploads exist; the bookkeeping does not.
The caller (an offline pass over /user/myPublishedSubtitles) knows path, stream position, language and SubDL id, and this endpoint writes exactly the row the uploader would have written: Status = uploaded with the id that makes the single deletable once the pack replaces it. It never touches SubDL itself and never uploads anything.

member.summary: F-M58 (09.09.2026): classifies a 429 response. SubDL uses TWO different 429 variants: (a) the real daily quota limit and (b) a transient server overload with body {"error":"service_busy","message":"Temporarily overloaded, retry shortly","retryAfterSeconds":5} — verified live 09.09.2026 while the panel showed only 24/2000 requests used. member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.SubdlApiClient.ReadQuotaAsync(System.Boolean,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
F-M238: reads the two counters the 429 decision needs and reports what they say about the direction that just hit a 429.
The status code alone cannot answer this: SubDL answers 429 both when the daily allowance is gone AND when a short-term rate limit tripped while plenty of quota remained. The counters are the only thing that tells the two apart, and the reset_at they carry is the timestamp a next-day fire must not undercut.
"Unreadable" is returned as its own answer rather than folded into "not exhausted", because the two call for opposite reactions: an unknown allowance retries at the day-long pace, an available one is ridden out within the hour.
member.param: True for the download counter, false for search/upload.
member.returns: What the counters say about this direction.

member.summary:
Gets the User-Agent the plugin's HTTP clients carry: the product name plus the REAL assembly version.
Until 10.10.2026 this was the fixed literal "Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlSync/1.0", so every release since 1.0 introduced itself to SubDL as version 1.0 — the server could not tell two versions apart, and the string named the assembly rather than the product. Read from the assembly, so a version bump needs no second edit and cannot fall out of step with it.
WHO SEES IT — traced through the tree on 10.10.2026, three counterparties: api.subdl.com (search, login, quota read, status probe), dl.subdl.com (the subtitle file download) and api.themoviedb.org. The last one is not an oversight: BuildApiClient's HttpClient is handed to TmdbImdbResolver, and SubdlStatusController's probe client serves the TMDb configuration probe as well. Both services sit behind a TLS-terminating front, so the operator and its edge read the header; the plugin's own log, Jellyfin itself, the LAN and the ISP do not. The operator decided on 10.10.2026 that TMDb may see it too — the agent says where a call comes from, and that is as true of an id lookup as of a subtitle search.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.SubdlApiClient.UserAgent
member.summary: Gets or sets the SubDL user-agent used for all requests.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.SubdlApiClient.NewHttpClient(System.Nullable{System.TimeSpan})
member.summary:
Creates an HttpClient that identifies itself as this plugin on every call it makes.
F-M343: the plugin builds HttpClient instances at more than one place — the main API client through BuildApiClient, and ad-hoc ones in the status probe, the quota read, the upload postprocessing controller and the upload pipeline's own pass. Those ad-hoc clients carried no agent at all, so their calls (login in particular, which adds no per-request header) went out with no User-Agent whatsoever. One factory keeps them from drifting apart again.
Not every client built here is a SubDL caller: SubdlStatusController holds one and uses it for the SubDL search probe AND the TMDb configuration probe, so TMDb sees this agent too. That is intended — see for who sees it and why.
member.param: Optional client timeout; the BCL default is left in place when null.
member.returns: The client, owned by the caller.

member.name: F:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.SubdlApiClient.IntegrationClientName
member.summary: The integration name this plugin reports to SubDL: "other". See for why this value and not another.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.SubdlApiClient.IntegrationClient
member.summary:
Gets or sets the integration name sent as client on the search call.
SubDL documents the accepted values — bazarr, stremio, kodi, subdl_player, custom_integration, other (subdl.com/api-doc, read 10.10.2026) — and the parameter is listed for the subtitles search ONLY, which is why it is not added to the upload or download calls. This plugin has no entry of its own, so it reports "other": the honest value, rather than claiming custom_integration, a category the operator did not choose. A dedicated value is SubDL's call, not ours.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.SubdlApiClient.DeletePublishedSubtitleAsync(System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
Performs the 3-step upload: getNId → uploadSingleSubtitle → uploadSubtitle (F-M8).
is the source quality the metadata step reports (F-M344). It is a parameter and no longer a literal: the documented values are web, bluray, dvd, hdtv and cam, and only the caller knows where the subtitle it hands over came from. See for the value list and the recognition rule.

F-M391 (operator order 02.11.2026): deletes ONE published subtitle of our own account by its SubDL id — the step that makes room for the pack a single is about to be absorbed into.
The order is deliberate and comes from the operator: the duplicate goes FIRST, then the pack is built from what is left, so the pack upload never competes with an entry that carries the same content. deleteSubtitle is NOT the route for this — measured 02.11.2026, it answers {"status": true, "subtitle deleted"} for a published entry and deletes nothing.
member.param: SubDL id of the entry to delete.
member.returns: True when SubDL confirmed the deletion.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.SubdlApiClient.ReportBrokenSubtitleAsync(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: F-M450: files one report about a subtitle on SubDL. The endpoint is the site's own report form (POST /report, Bearer from the login the upload path already performs); it is not part of the documented API, so every answer is read defensively: only success:true counts, a 429 is reported back as "deferred" so the caller can keep the row for the next run, and anything else is a plain failure that must not be retried in a loop.
member.param: One of the four SubDL categories.
member.returns: Accepted, deferred (rate limited) or failed.

member.summary:
F-M372: the three-step upload for a whole season — one object on SubDL's side instead of one per episode.
The Upload API documents the shape: uploadSingleSubtitle takes ONE file per call, uploadSubtitle then takes the array file_n_ids, and for packed multi-file uploads the name field becomes the zip name on download. The container is therefore built by SubDL, never by us; what we send is the files plus the claim is_full_season=true and the episode range in ef/ee.
member.param: Episode files, ascending: the name each subtitle carries and its text.
SubDL language code (one pack = one language).
Release names of the season's episodes — the array SubDL stores is exactly why a pack can carry them all.
HI/SDH variant — a pack never mixes both sides.
member.returns: Success with the raw response attached; the caller reads the pack id from it.

member.summary:
V2 single-file download by nId — GET /api/v2/subtitles/{nId}/download?format=file (Bearer auth). Same retry contract as v1 downloads (429/5xx backoff, F-M27/F-M58).
F-M450 (09.11.2026): many subtitles have no single file at all — the endpoint then answers 409 not_a_single_file and says what to do: ask for ?format=zip. Measured on a night's rejects: every one of them was such a case, and the archive carried exactly the .srt that had just been thrown away. So the fallback is part of the download now — fetch the zip and unpack the file for the wanted season/episode.
member.param: Wanted season for the archive fallback (0 = none).
Wanted episode for the archive fallback (0 = none).
member.returns: What this attempt produced, with its own status — never state on the client.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.SubdlApiClient.ListMyPublishedSubtitlesAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Int32,System.Func{Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.OwnSubtitleEntry,System.Boolean},System.Action{System.Int32})
member.summary: F-M17y: lists the user's own uploads (rejected and accepted) from SubDL. Used to clean up the dashboard after a duplicate upload verdict. IMPORTANT: SubDL's /user/mySubtitles ignores page/per_page/offset/limit entirely and always returns the same complete list (verified 2026-09-24: page=1/2, per_page=10/100/500, offset=100/252, limit, start all returned byte-identical payloads, no pagination headers). Iterating "pages" therefore re-reads the same entries N times, which silently inflated the postprocessing counters (5 x 650 = 3250 "fetched" instead of the real 650). We keep the loop for forward compatibility, but deduplicate by UploadId and stop at the first page that adds no new id, so the returned list and the reported totals are truthful.

F-M432 (operator order 03.11.2026: "Bau für filme denselben id grep wie für packs oder Einzelepisoden auch"): reads the account's PUBLISHED list, newest first.
/user/mySubtitles was the only source of an upload id, and it lists only what is still awaiting review — measured on 03.11.2026 it was empty while the account had 8268 published subtitles. The published list carries the same id per entry (subtitle.id), 25 per page, newest first, so a freshly uploaded subtitle is on page 1. For a movie there is no season or episode to match on, so the release name is the only handle — exactly the way a pack is matched.
member.param: How many pages to read (25 entries each).
member.returns: The entries, newest first; null when the call fails.
member.summary: F-M437 (operator decision 04.11.2026): the walk is WATERMARKED, not fixed. The list comes newest first, so a caller that knows how far it read last time stops as soon as a page has reached older entries — a daily pass then costs a handful of pages instead of the whole account.
member.param: Ceiling for one walk (a catch-up run after a pause needs more pages).
Called with the OLDEST entry of each page after it was added; true ends the walk before the next page is requested.
Reports each page number actually fetched, so the caller can log the depth.
member.returns: The entries read, newest first; null when the first call failed.

member.summary:
F-M387: EVERY unpack file that belongs to this season/episode, in listing order — the retry list a QA gate walks before the candidate is thrown away. A pack can carry several files for the same episode (a plain and an SDH one, two release variants), and a verdict on the first says nothing about the second.
The hearing-impaired filter is the operator's rule (02.11.2026: "sdh sollte nur mit sdh gematcht werden"): with set, only files whose own flag equals it are returned. A plain request never falls back to an SDH file and vice versa — the two are different tracks, and swapping them silently changes what the viewer gets.

member.returns: Matching files, best match first; empty when the listing has none.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.SubtitleCandidate.FoldStyledLetters(System.String)
member.summary: F-M457: folds styled Unicode letters and digits to ASCII — the mathematical alphanumerics (bold/italic/script/fraktur/double-struck/sans-serif/monospace) and the fullwidth forms that East-Asian releases use. Deliberately arithmetic instead of a Unicode normalisation call: needs ICU and throws under invariant globalization, which a Jellyfin host may well run. Each style block carries its 52 letter slots in order (A–Z then a–z), even where Unicode leaves a slot unassigned because a letterlike character stands in for it, so an offset maps cleanly; the digits come in runs of ten, so a modulo ten reads them all.
member.returns: The same name with the styling folded away.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.SubdlQuota.PendingReasonForWorker(Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSchedulerCoordinator,System.String)
member.summary:
The LOCAL deferral state for the answer: every worker that has a deferred fire pending, with the moment it is due (F-M288/F-M294, reworked 03.10.2026).
The server counters cannot express this. They can read 3/1000 while a worker is already deferred, so a box built from them alone shows blue bars and no hint that nothing will run for the next quarter of an hour. The values come from the scheduler's pending fires — the same source the Workers list and the server log read, so all three agree.
The user's rule (03.10.2026): "defer whenever a fire was scheduled, whichever worker". So this is not limited to the two directions — the database refresh, the OSHash refresh and postprocessing carry fires of their own and are named by their own worker name.
The reason comes from the worker's own stored row, passed through verbatim rather than summarised: a deferral is a run-lock push just as often as it is a rate limit, and a label saying "rate limit" on a lock deferral would send the reader looking for a quota problem that does not exist.
member.returns: The deferred workers, each with its short name, cause and due moment; empty when nothing is deferred.
member.summary: F-M475: the reason of the PENDING attempt that belongs to this worker, or null when the worker has no pending fire (or is not one of the two directions). Kept out of the note loop so the loop itself stays direction-blind — every worker runs through the same pass (F-M436).
member.param: The scheduler, or null while the plugin is still starting.
member.returns: The reason text, or null.

member.summary: F-M352: what the status line says about directions and maintenance workers that do not run on their own — "off" for a direction that cannot start at all, "manual" for a worker whose cadence is Manual (its dashboard button still runs it).
member.returns: One string per switched-off or manual-only worker, in the order the operator named them.

member.summary:
F-M238: the two SubDL allowances, read from GET /api/v2/me — the same numbers the settings page shows, so GUI and pipeline can never disagree.
Search and download are SEPARATE allowances with separate limits. A run can be out of downloads while search has plenty left (and the reverse), so every decision names the direction it means instead of asking "is the quota gone".
is the server's own reset timestamp. It is the floor for a next-day fire: the retry must never be scheduled before it, because before it the allowance is still spent and the fire would only burn another request.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.TmdbImdbResolver
member.summary: Resolves an IMDb ID from a TMDB id via the TMDB REST API (user decision 08.09.2026). REQUIRED component (F-M203, 01.10.2026): with no key configured a run does not start at all — both pipelines refuse it up front and name the missing field (F-M19). The reason it is not optional: id resolution is TMDb-authoritative in both directions, so without it an episode id could reach SubDL where a show id belongs. Results are cached per (tmdbId, isSeries, year, season, episode) for the process lifetime (negative results too — avoids hammering TMDB while polling).

member.summary: F-M190 (24.09.2026): resolves a title WITHOUT assuming the media type — TMDB's own answer decides whether it is a film or a series, and the season/episode numbers come from the file name. This is the watchdog's proven approach and the only one that works when an episode sits in a library typed "movies" (Jellyfin then reports it as a Movie and a film-only search finds nothing).
member.param: Title or series name from the file NAME.
True when the name carried a series marker.
member.returns: Ids plus the type TMDB actually returned, or nulls.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.TmdbImdbResolver.ResolveByTitleYearAsync(System.String,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
F-M231 (27.09.2026, user decision "Wir testen jfs id immer gegen tmdb"): the STRICT twin of — it answers only when a hit's OWN year equals the year asked for. No year match means NOT FOUND, never a fallback to the most popular hit.
This is what tests a Jellyfin id against TMDb. The ordinary multi-search falls back to the first hit, so it cannot tell "TMDb agrees" from "TMDb found something else"; against an item whose metadata pins the wrong title it silently confirms the pinned id. Measured 27.09.2026: a 110-minute 2026 film sitting in Mayday/S01/ carries tmdb=90 (the 2003 documentary) in its tvshow.nfo, and the pair check passes because 90 really does resolve to that imdb id — the title and year were never asked. Used with the year from the FILE NAME it returns the 2026 film instead (tmdb=1137844).

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.TmdbImdbResolver.HandleAuthFailure
member.summary: Handles the 401 case: report once (Normal level via event) and switch into AuthBroken mode — every further call short-circuits to null without a request.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.TmdbImdbResolver.VerifyIdsAgainstTmdbAsync(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
F-M231 (27.09.2026, user decision "Wir testen jfs id immer gegen tmdb"): tests Jellyfin's ids against TMDb by TITLE and YEAR, and corrects them only when TMDb answers with a hit whose own year matches exactly.
Why a separate step: checks that the two ids belong to the same entity, which is tautological — a wrongly pinned pair passes it (tmdb 90 ⇄ tt0386950 both describe the same series, so "they agree"). Title and year were never asked, and that is what lets a 110-minute 2026 film sitting under Mayday/S01/ keep the 2003 documentary's identity through a whole run.
Conservative by construction: no exact year match ⇒ Jellyfin's ids are kept unchanged. The step only ever ADDS a correction, so a missing year or a title TMDb spells differently costs nothing.
member.returns: Ids, the type TMDb reported, and whether a correction was applied.

member.summary: Last-resort path (user decision 08.09.2026): no IMDB and no TMDB id after the metadata wait → search TMDB by title (+year), take the best match and resolve its IMDb ID. Returns null when no key, no result, or no IMDB linked.
member.param: Movie title or SERIES name (never an episode title).
Release/first-air year for disambiguation or null.
True for tv, false for movie.
member.returns: IMDb ID (tt…) or null.
member.summary: (user decision 12.09.2026): IMDb→TMDB backfill. An item with an IMDb id but no TMDB id gets its TMDB id via /find/{imdb}?external_source=imdb_id so uploads carry the tmdb_id metadata on SubDL. Cached like the forward lookup; null on miss/failure (uploads proceed with imdb alone — never blocking).

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.TmdbImdbResolver.ResolveSeriesByEpisodeAsync(System.String,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Int32)
member.summary: F-M347 (11.10.2026, operator decision): resolves a SERIES from its title plus the season and episode its file name states — by asking the episode itself instead of trusting a title hit.
member.remarks: Why: 61 of 70 series NAMES carry no year (measured on 1224 names from SubDL's latest list), so the strict title+year test, which needs a year, can never run for them, and the loose path then falls back to TMDb's FIRST hit — right only 4 times out of 14 measured. The episode is the better witness: a show either has that episode or it does not. No candidate with the episode means no resolution — never a guess.
member.param: Series name as parsed from the file name.
Season number from the file name.
Episode number from the file name.
How many search hits to test; each test is one call.
member.returns: Ids of the first candidate that really has that episode, or nulls.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.TmdbImdbResolver.FindShowByImdbAsync(System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: F-M191 (24.09.2026): what is this IMDb id — an episode or the show itself? TMDB's /find answers tv_episode_results for an episode (its "show_id" IS the series TMDB id) and tv_results for the show. Verified live: tt38949652 → episode S1E10 of show 291084 (Best Medicine), tt21289596 → S3E3 of 95480 (Slow Horses), tt6037988 → the show itself (Last Seen, 258230).
member.returns: (seriesTmdbId, isEpisode) or (null,false) when TMDB knows nothing.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.TmdbImdbResolver.ResolveShowByEpisodeIdAsync(System.String,System.String,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
F-M202 (25.09.2026, user decision): Jellyfin carries an EPISODE TMDB id and the file name carries season/episode — together they prove which SHOW the file belongs to. /find cannot walk an episode id up (verified: find?external_source=tmdb_id returns EMPTY), but the episode id can be CONFIRMED from the other side: search the title from the FILE NAME, walk to that show's S/E, and accept the show only when the episode id there equals Jellyfin's id. Measured on the test library: 9/9 exact matches (Best Medicine S1E1 → 6676484, … S2E1 → 7530224, Last Seen S1E1 → 7321029).
This closes the gap F-M191 left open: with no IMDb id and only an episode TMDB id, the 10 affected files had no path to a show id at all.
SAFETY — this is NEVER a guess. Title search can return several shows ("Last Seen" also matches "Last Seen On Holiday", "Last Seen Alive"); the episode-id equality check is the only thing that makes the mapping provable. No confirmed match ⇒ (null, null) ⇒ the item is skipped, exactly like any other unresolvable series.
member.param: Jellyfin's TMDB id, known to be an EPISODE id.
Series title taken from the FILE NAME.
Season number from the file name.

F-M151 (20.09.2026): upload ID quality gate. Validates and/or corrects the IMDb/TMDB IDs that Jellyfin reports for a media item. Missing IDs are filled via TMDB, conflicting IDs are corrected towards the TMDB source of truth, and items that cannot be resolved at all return nulls so the caller can skip them.
For episodes this always operates on the SERIES level (tvshow IMDB/TMDB), never the episode IMDB — the SubDL upload metadata requires series id + season + episode.

F-M28a: cross-checks and corrects Jellyfin's ids via TMDb whenever a key is configured.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.TransientRetryHandler
member.summary:
F-M235: tolerates a transport timeout three times before giving up, and never retries a user stop.
A timeout is a transient condition, exactly like the 5xx login answer handled in F-M232 — the server may simply be slow. Before this, an expired request threw TaskCanceledException, which the API clients do not catch (they catch JsonException only), so it travelled up into the run loop's catch (OperationCanceledException) and was reported as "cancelled — keeping the partial result". A slow server therefore looked like the user pressing stop, and the item was silently dropped without a retry.
The two cancellations must be told apart, and only one source of truth can do it: the token the CALLER passed. If that token is already cancelled the user (or the run) asked us to stop, and repeating the request would make the stop button ineffective. If it is still alive, the cancel came from this handler's own per-attempt timeout and the request is worth repeating.

member.summary: Per-request override of the attempt timeout. A subtitle archive is orders of magnitude larger than a JSON answer, so the caller raises the budget for a file download instead of letting one global value decide for both.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.TvSubtitlesClient
member.summary:
F-M480 (operator order 15.11.2026): the tvsubtitles.net client — the second source, and the only one that is reached by reading its web pages rather than by an API. The site has NO API: /api*, /xmlrpc.php and api.tvsubtitles.net all answer 404/DNS (measured 15.11.2026), only /rss.xml exists and carries no per-episode data.
The path is fixed and it is the site's own navigation: /add.html (show list) → /tvshow-<id>.html (seasons) → /tvshow-<id>-<season>.html (episode pages) → /episode-<id>.html (entries) → /subtitle-<id>.html → /download-<id>.html (the file name sits in JavaScript fragments) → the ZIP under files/.
WHAT THIS CLASS IS AND IS NOT: it is the source's method surface — resolve, list, fetch, build an upload, send an upload. It is NOT wired into the pipelines: the switches for this source report "kein Anbieter verbaut" (F-M478) until a caller exists. Keeping the client separate from the wiring is the point: the protocol can be tested against captured pages without a download run.
Every parser is static and takes the HTML as a string, so the suites can drive them with the captured pages under scripts/tests/tvsubtitles/fixtures instead of the live site.

member.summary:
F-M480: parses the entries of an episode page.
The language is NOT in the text — the only trustworthy carrier is the flag image, and it must be read per BLOCK (from one subtitle anchor up to the next), because a bare search finds the flag of the following entry and mislabels the current one. member.summary: F-M480: is this payload a ZIP already? The site serves the archive straight from the download URL in one of its two shapes; the local header ("PK\u0003\u0004") is what tells them apart without trusting a content type the site does not always set.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Api.TvSubtitlesClient.DownloadAsync(System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
F-M480: fetches one subtitle and returns the first .srt out of the ZIP.
The bytes are handed over UNTOUCHED: the site serves UTF-8 next to cp1250, cp1251, cp1253, cp1254 and cp1256 depending on the language, and guessing here would repeat the codepage defect that made Russian, Greek and Arabic unreadable in the library on 15.11.2026. Decoding is the pipeline's business, not the transport's.
member.returns: The member name inside the ZIP and the raw bytes.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.MinCallPauseSec

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.DownloadRefetchInterval
member.summary: Gets or sets the v2 match_score threshold in percent (, user decision 15.09.2026). Main path downloads only candidates with API match_score >= this value. Default 80 (0.80).

Gets or sets the download refetch/rhythm interval — per-item refetch gap AND the download rhythm (F-M47/F-M57). DEFAULT: Weekly (user decision 09.09.2026). OBSOLETE since F-M111 — kept for XML compat, replaced by RefetchInterval.

members.member:
Gets or sets THE unified refetch interval (F-M111, user decision 12.09.2026): one rhythm for both directions — per-item refetch gap AND the scheduled cycle tick. GUI: General section. Migration: defaults to Weekly.
F-M210: every scheduled job is driven by its OWN setting; this one governs ONLY the pipeline cycles.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.DownloadQaRetryLimit
member.summary:
F-M320 (operator order 08.10.2026): how many candidates may be FETCHED hoping for a correction the alignment can prove against the audio — the correction hunt's budget (F-M318).
It used to be a give-up counter: N saveless runs of a (item, language) pair closed the pair without any SubDL search or fetch until a save succeeded. That is gone. The operator's rule is that this limit bounds the FIT, not the other gates — a gate rejection (language, structure, min-cues, runtime) is a verdict on the candidate, not a budget, and the walk simply moves on. What still bounds a hopeless file is the download budget per run (F-M50) plus the burned-release memory (F-M200), neither of which hides a live file.
0 means no cap on the correction hunt. Default: 3.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.QaDownloadMinCues
member.summary: (user decision 11.09.2026): download QA gate — minimum cue count (≥30, same F-M16 threshold as upload). Catches valid-but-stub SRTs (parseable but A handful of cues on a 2 h film). Rejects are memorized. Default: true.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.QaDownloadVerifyLanguage
member.summary: (user decision 11.09.2026): download QA gate — language verification (same F-M15 logic as upload: CLD2 content detection vs stream tag, family exceptions MS/EU/GL/CA/DA/NO). Fail-open when CLD2 has no verdict. Default: true.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.AllowAiTranslatedSubs
member.summary:
F-M296 (development): download auto-sync — shift a fetched subtitle by the single constant offset measured against the audio, before it is saved.
A downloaded subtitle is frequently whole seconds off: the release's own timing does not match this rip. The offset is measurable to about 0.2 s (planted shifts of −3 / +2 / +4 / +8 / +12 s came back as −3.20 / +1.80 / +3.80 / +7.80 / +11.80 s), and a large constant shift is NOT mistaken for drift, which is what makes a correction possible at all.
The corrected file is written as usual AND the untouched original is kept beside it as the one-entry archive <name>.<lang>.srt.unsynced.zip (F-M306). Registered is the hash of the CORRECTED file, so the duplicate guard sees exactly what lies on disk. A file whose offset MOVES is repaired by the staircase of F-M300, not by a single offset — no average over a drift is ever applied.
F-M300 (development): a DRIFTING file is no longer refused. The segments the gate found are the repair — each cue is shifted by the offset of its own segment, a staircase — which took the worst-cue residual over 36 drifting episodes from a 10.74 s median to 4.51 s, 33 of 36 better. Two of the 36 come out worse and no reference-free signal separates them, so a same-language reference (F-M297) is preferred when one exists and the untouched original is kept either way.
On by default. The cost is one full audio decode per saved file — measured at 11 s wall / 21 s CPU for a 49 min HEVC episode on the Pi 5 — and the run shares one decode between the drift gate and this switch when both are on. A staircase adds no second decode; it is the same verdict applied per segment.
Default: true.

F-M449: whether subtitles uploaded by the machine-translation account (SUBDL AI) may downloaded. Off by default — the switch is applied to the SEARCH RESULT, so such a candidate neither enters the ranking nor costs a download unit.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.ReportBrokenSubtitles
member.summary: F-M450: report a subtitle that failed twice (download delivered no data, or the file did not pass the content gates) to SubDL, using its own report form. On by default; one report per subtitle and defect, ever, and only after the second failed attempt.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.QaDownloadAutoSync
member.summary: F-M303: Korrektur ist EIN Abschnitt mit EINEM Schalter — kein Zwischenkopf, die Beschreibung gehört an den Schalter.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.RefreshLibraryAfterDownload
member.summary: F-M473: whether a download run that saved subtitles tells Jellyfin about them, so they show up right away. On by default. Only the written files are reported — the server looks for new and updated files in precisely those paths, never a full database scan. A run that saved nothing reports nothing.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.QaDownloadAudioTrackByLanguage
member.summary:
F-M296 (development): the audio track an audio-reading gate decodes, chosen by LANGUAGE rather than by stream order.
Priority: (1) a track in the subtitle's own language, (2) English, (3) the first track without a language tag, else the first track. Measured on 304 files with sidecar subtitles, this picks a different track than the first in 34 of 387 (file, language) cases (~9 %) — typically an Italian release whose first track is the Italian dub, with the English original on track 1. 76 files carry no language tag on their first track at all.
The effect on the VERDICT is small (both tracks of the one multi-track file measured closely agreed: span 17.4 vs. 18.1 s); what the switch removes is the assumption that the first track is the right one, which is measurably false.
Default: true.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.AllocateMissingLanguageCodes
member.summary:
F-M261 (user decision 30.09.2026): allocate missing language codes to the media files themselves. Expert / General.
A subtitle track with no language tag, or the literal und/undefined, cannot be mapped: invents the code UN through its two-letter fallback, and a null tag produces no registry row at all. Either way every reader of the embedded area is answered from nothing — the language reads as absent for a track that is right there, and the item is queued and searched for what it already carries.
With this on, the seeder resolves those tracks (one ffmpeg pass per file, F-M5), applies the 2 KB floor and the offline detector (QaGates.DetectLanguage), writes the found language back into the container as a real track tag, and records the file under its NEW hash together with the languages it now carries. What the detector cannot decide is left WITHOUT a tag on purpose: a wrong language would claim coverage the file does not have.
This is one switch and not two, because the two halves are not independent: the file was already re-read to detect the language, and a language written into the file is the only form other tools can see. The write is what makes the file change identity, so the gate runs before the hash and the file is re-registered under it (see ).
Default: false. Measured on a 525 MB episode with 44 text tracks: extraction 0.8 s, detection 13.7 s, tag write 29.9 s — the write dominates because the container is copied through. It runs once per file and never again, but a first pass over an untagged library is a long task and must not be the default.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.ArrivalDebounceMinutes
member.summary: (user decision 11.09.2026): ItemAdded debounce window in minutes — how long the arrival watcher waits after the first event before running the cycle (download first, then upload), so that files arriving together (season import, NAS sync) are processed in ONE cycle. (user decision 02.11.2026): default back to 5 — the shorter windows split a slow NAS import into several cycles, and the operator prefers one pass.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.JobSpacingMinutes
member.summary: (user decision 14.09.2026): when a due job (anchor fire, recovery fire, event batch, prune) finds the global run lock busy, the scheduler does NOT drop it — it defers the job by this many minutes and retries on the next tick after the new due time. Default: 15.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.SearchMaxPages
member.summary: (user request 14.09.2026): number of pages fetched per SubDL API search (10 results per page server-side). Applies to the download Search. (user decision 14.09.2026): default 3 — all wanted languages go in ONE call (server-side filter, Early-stop) so 3 pages = 30 results is normally plenty; deeper digging is opt-in. Clamp 1–100.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.DownloadDryRun
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the download pipeline runs in dry-run mode (no file writes, no external subs placed).

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.DownloadArchiveCacheDays
member.summary: Gets or sets how many days a downloaded archive is kept on disk (F-M370). A season pack serves one episode per run, and the free daily limit is 50 downloads, so the same pack is asked for again on the following days — on disk it is answered without a request. Measured 01.11.2026: 51 archive fetches for 45 files, 26 of them on three packs. 0 turns the disk cache off (user decision 01.11.2026, Download tab).

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.DownloadArchiveCacheMaxMb
member.summary: Gets or sets the size ceiling of the archive cache in megabytes (F-M370). When the cache grows past it the oldest archives are dropped first. 0 turns the disk cache off as well — either switch at 0 disables it (user decision 01.11.2026: 512 MB default).

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.FfmpegPath
member.summary: (user decision 20.09.2026): override for the ffmpeg executable path used to extract embedded text subtitles. Empty means auto-detect: Jellyfin's configured encoder path first, then "ffmpeg" in PATH, then common system locations.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.DownloadContinueAfterLimit
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the DOWNLOAD pipeline waits out a daily SubDL limit hit and then continues (F-M49). Downloads can hit TWO quotas: the account-wide API request quota (2,000/day free tier) AND the download quota (~50/day via direct dl.subdl.com links) — a 429 from either stops the run when this is off. Default off: the run stops; remaining items keep their refetch clock and the next scheduled run picks them up. On: the run waits (once per run, at most 24 h) until the server-reported reset time and retries the current candidate; a second 429 in the same run stops.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.UploadContinueAfterLimit
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the UPLOAD pipeline waits out the account-wide SubDL API request quota (2,000/day free tier, HTTP 429) once per run and continues after the server-reported reset. Uploads draw only from the API quota (no download quota involved). Default off: the run stops; the next run picks up the remaining items. History: DownloadContinueAfterLimit → ContinueAfterDailyLimit (general, 08.09.2026 evening) → split into UploadContinueAfterLimit + DownloadContinueAfterLimit (user decision: download can hit TWO quotas — API requests AND ~50 downloads/day — while upload only hits the API quota).

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.UploadPostprocessDelayMinutes
member.summary:
F-M445 (Betreiber-Entscheidung 02.11.2026): Vorlaufzeit des Upload-Nachlaufs nach dem Ende eines Upload-Laufs, in Minuten. **0 schaltet den Nachlauf ab** — dann wird nie ein Termin gesetzt. Gültig sind 0..1440. **Es gibt keinen festen Anker mehr** — jeder beendete Upload-Lauf terminiert den Nachlauf neu auf „Laufende + diese Minuten", und der **letzte Auftrag gewinnt**: ein noch offener Termin wird überschrieben, nicht addiert. Läuft also Upload 1 um 12:15 aus, steht der Nachlauf auf 12:45; endet Upload 2 um 12:30, bleibt es bei 12:45 (12:30 + 30 = 13:00 wird NICHT addiert, sondern der bestehende Auftrag storniert und neu terminiert — der letzte Lauf bestimmt den Termin).
Der Grund: der Handle-Remap Upload-Id → Eintrags-Id und das Wegräumen abgelehnter Uploads hingen vorher am Tagesanker und liefen damit erst am nächsten Morgen — ein Pack, das am selben Tag gebaut wurde, löschte seine Einzeluploads noch mit der Upload-Id, die deletePublishedSubtitle nicht kennt (F-M435: 3758706 = Eintrag, 380828 = Upload).

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.PostprocessMaxPages
member.summary: F-M176: max mySubtitles pages fetched per postprocessing run. Default 5.

F-M437 (operator decision 04.11.2026): the CEILING of the page walk, not its length. The walk stops at ; this value only bounds a catch-up run after a long gap, so it must be large enough to reach the bottom of a big list (25 entries per page).

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.PostprocessWatermarkUtc
member.summary: F-M437: the newest createdAt the last pass has already walked, stored as the account reported it. The next pass pages down only until it reaches entries older than this, so a daily pass costs a handful of pages instead of the whole list — and a pass after a pause catches up by itself.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.MissingCredentials
member.summary:
F-M19/F-M203: the four credentials the plugin cannot run without, in ONE place so both pipelines and the settings page answer the same question.
They are not alternatives: the SubDL login pair authenticates the UPLOAD (its three steps carry a Bearer token from /login), the SubDL API key authenticates search, file download and the quota read, and the TMDb key is what resolves and corrects the ids in both directions. A missing one is not a degraded mode, it is a run that cannot do its job — so the run is refused up front with the field named, instead of failing later at the first call that needs it.
member.returns: The human-readable labels of every missing credential; empty when complete.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.TmdbApiKey
member.summary: Gets or sets the REQUIRED TMDB API key (v3), the TMDb-authoritative source for id resolution (F-M202/F-M203, user decision 25.09.2026). It resolves missing IMDb/TMDb ids, corrects Jellyfin's ids, and decides film vs series. Empty/null → nothing runs: a run without the key is refused up front (F-M203), because the id resolution it feeds is not optional in either direction. The GUI refuses to save an empty key.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration.QaOwnUploadCheck

Kept for deserialization only; the value is no longer read by any code path. Since F-M184 the duplicate decision happens in postprocessing (mySubtitles sweep).

ON: the detected language replaces the tag and the stream uploads normally; detection failure → skip. OFF: every 'und' stream is removed from the upload set (skip, logged). Default: on.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.DbFiles
member.summary:
The one place that knows how the plugin's data files are spelled.
The file is a path, not a label — every read and write resolves it here, so a rename is one edit instead of a hunt for string literals.
Renamed twice, and both times for a reason worth keeping. It was subdl-sync.db until 28.09.2026 (the name kept the plugin's working title), and subdl-scribe.db until 08.10.2026, when the store became SQLite and the extension stopped being decorative: the file is now a real SQLite database, so it says so — subdl-scribe.sqlite. The old name is not reused as a second live file: it is the IMPORT source, read once and renamed aside (F-M327).

member.summary: The data file's name.

member.summary: The name the data file carried before it became SQLite. Kept ONLY as the import source (F-M327) — nothing reads or writes it as a live store any more.

member.name: F:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.DbFiles.SideSuffixes
member.summary: Suffixes SQLite gives the files sitting NEXT TO a database. Built from the FULL file name, not its stem: subdl-scribe.sqlite → subdl-scribe.sqlite-wal. This is the opposite of the convention the previous engine used, which is why still exists as a separate helper rather than a shared string.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.DbFiles.PathIn(System.String)
member.summary: Full path of the data file inside a plugin data directory.

member.summary: Full path of the PREVIOUS data file, the one-time import source. Never the live store.
member.returns: Absolute path of the old document store.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.DbFiles.SidePath(System.String,System.String)
member.summary:
Path of a side file belonging to a data file. SQLite appends the suffix to the FULL name: subdl-scribe.sqlite → subdl-scribe.sqlite-wal. Appending to the stem (subdl-scribe-wal) matches nothing SQLite ever writes.
The previous engine did the opposite — it built side names from the stem — so this helper carries a comment on each side rather than an assumption on either.
member.param: Suffix including the leading dash, e.g. "-wal".
member.returns: Absolute path of the side file.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubtitleStatus
member.summary:
The four states a subtitle can be in. Everything else is derived.
There is deliberately no "settled"/"done" state: "is this position finished?" is answered by the presence of one of the three stored states below. The previous model carried a separate settled row next to the outcome row, which duplicated every verdict and forced every reader to know both layers.

member.summary: The subtitle was uploaded to SubDL.

member.summary: The subtitle was not accepted. says by whom and why.

member.summary: The subtitle was downloaded from SubDL.

member.name: F:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubtitleStatus.Observed
member.summary:
F-M257: the track was SEEN, no verdict exists. Written by whoever reads the streams or the directory without doing anything about it (seeder scan, download pipeline) — it records the file fact (language, HI) and deliberately claims nothing else.
Needed because the embedded area had exactly ONE writer (the upload pipeline), so with UploadEnabled=false — the shipped default — no embedded row existed at all. A reader that depends on that area (the HI question, F-M254) then answered "HI absent" forever for a container that already carried the track, and nothing could ever correct it.
NOT terminal by design: and are verdicts that close a position, an observation is not. Every terminality check must keep filtering for the verdict values, otherwise this state would mark work as done that was never attempted.

Why a subtitle was rejected. Stored in so the verdict itself stays one state ().
The distinction that matters operationally is WHO rejected: a remote rejection is final and unactionable, a local quality rejection means the file itself could be improved, and a self-echo rejection only says "we already uploaded this pair in this run".

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubtitleState
member.summary: Shared state fields of a subtitle record, in both areas 2 and 3.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubtitleState.Language
member.summary: Two or three letter language code.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubtitleState.HearingImpaired
member.summary:
Hearing-impaired / SDH variant.
F-M285 (user decision 02.10.2026): the stored value is THREE-valued, not two. A row must say true or false EXPLICITLY; null means "this row does not say". The distinction is the whole point: a document store has no schema, so a row written before this field existed reads back as a default, and a default that looks like a decision is how a missing fact becomes a false claim. An explicit false is a statement (this subtitle is NOT the variant); a null is a gap that a backfill may fill and no reader may read.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubtitleState.Forced
member.summary:
F-M284 (user decision 02.10.2026): the track is FORCED — it carries the lines of foreign-language scenes, not the film's dialogue.
An Eigenschaft OF THIS DATUM, exactly like , and stored the same three-valued way (F-M285): true / false are statements, null is a row that does not say. It never counts as coverage, so a language whose only track is forced stays open and is searched for (F-M246).
Unlike the hearing-impaired flag it is not bilateral: Jellyfin reports it on its streams, but SubDL has no forced counterpart — no search filter, no response field, and 0 of 22 candidates named it when measured live on 02.10.2026. So a forced datum is OBSERVED, never sought, fetched or uploaded. Recording it is what stops it from being mistaken for the film's dialogue.

members.member:
Area 2, beneath the file: one row per embedded subtitle stream.
The key is (media hash, stream position) because that IS the identity of an embedded track — it has no name and no independent existence. Two streams of one file can share a language (a normal and an SDH variant, or two releases), so the language alone must never identify the row; conflating them is what made one rejected stream block all its siblings.
F-M197: one record per embedded subtitle stream, keyed by media hash + stream position. The position is the identity of a track: it has no name of its own, and two streams of one file can share a language (a normal and an SDH variant).

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.EmbedTrackEntity.Id
member.summary: Primary key: "<media hash>|<sub position>". A stable business key rather than a database-assigned id, so an upsert always updates the row it means to update.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.EmbedTrackEntity.MediaHash
member.summary: Parent media hash.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.EmbedTrackEntity.SubPos
member.summary: ffmpeg stream position (0:s:N).

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.EmbedTrackEntity.DetectionAttemptedAt
member.summary:
When language DETECTION last ran for this position, or null when it never did.
Detection is the expensive half of the gate (extraction plus classification), and for a track the detector cannot classify the answer never changes. Recording the attempt is what lets the next scan skip it instead of re-opening the media file: the seeder's cheap pre-check only asks whether an untagged track EXISTS, and a track that stays untagged passes that question forever. Per TRACK, not per file — a file can have one unresolved track beside forty settled ones.
A tag write gives the file a new hash and therefore fresh rows, which is the one event that should retry. Set by the gate, read by the gate and by the refresh worker.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.EmbedTrackEntity.DetectionOutcome
member.summary: How the last detection attempt ended — one of , else null.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.DetectionOutcome

member.summary: The track held less text than the 2 KB floor — a verdict would be garbage.

member.name: F:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.DetectionOutcome.Failed

members.member:
Area 3: one row per loose .srt sidecar file.
Keyed by the normalized CONTENT hash rather than by name or language. That is what makes a sidecar an independent thing: the same subtitle text stays "known" when the file is renamed or moved, and two sidecars that share a language but differ in content stay two rows instead of collapsing into one. The filename is kept for reference only and deliberately plays no part in the identity.
F-M199: one record per loose .srt file, keyed by the normalized content hash (F-M186), so a sidecar stays known after a rename or a move, and two sidecars differing in text stay two rows.

members.member:
Area 4: download candidates that were fetched and then discarded, remembered per (item, language) so the same candidate is never fetched and screened twice.
Kept apart from areas 2 and 3 because its grain is neither a stream nor a piece of content — it is "this remote release id was burned for this file and language". SubDL's own id is the only identifier such a verdict has.
F-M200: one record per fetched-and-discarded candidate, keyed by item id + language + SubDL id. Its grain is "this remote release was burned for this file and language".

member.summary:
Cumulative subtitle counters shown in the configuration GUI.
These used to live in the plugin configuration XML (F-M23), which meant they were stored next to user settings while the data they describe lives in the database — so a database reset left them untouched and the display drifted away from the data it claimed to report (measured 25.09.2026: after a reset the database held 311 uploaded rows while the display still said 743). They now live in the database, which makes them part of the same reset and incapable of drifting.
Single row, fixed key "status" — this is a running total, not a per-item record.

member.summary: Fixed primary key.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.StatusStatsEntity.RejectedDownload
member.summary: F-M286: candidates FETCHED and then thrown away, per direction — every reject path, not the QA gates alone. Renamed from QaRejectedDownload when the meaning widened: a fetched candidate discarded because its content was already known, or because no usable bytes came back, spends a request just like a gate rejection does. Reconciles with the day's quota: requests = saved + rejected. Nothing that was never fetched is counted.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.StatusStatsEntity.RejectedUpload
member.summary: F-M286: upload candidates discarded before or instead of an upload — QA gates, und-off, unmapped language, self-echo, duplicate-remote, forced (F-M284). Same rule as the download: one field, every reject path.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.StatusStatsEntity.FittedToAudio
member.summary: F-M308: downloaded subtitles that were FITTED to their audio track — the correction applied, not merely offered. The volume counter counts subtitles that arrived; this one counts the ones the run had to move, which is why it is reported next to the corrections and not next to the volume. Download only: the upload direction has no audio fit.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.StatusStatsEntity.BrokenReported
member.summary: F-M455 (operator order 10.11.2026: "Neues Statistikfeld Download: Broken subtitle reported to SubDL nach Auto-Sync"): subtitles this run reported to SubDL as broken — a file that failed its content gates or answered empty TWICE, and whose report the portal confirmed. It sits directly behind the Auto-Sync row because it belongs to the same story: the fit measures the file, and when the measurement says the upload is broken, this is where the answer goes. Only an accepted report counts; a deferred or refused one is not a report.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.StatusStatsEntity.LanguageCodesAllocated
member.summary: F-M311: media FILES whose language codes were written by the seeder's allocation pass — not a download and not an upload. One count is one file that got at least one real tag where it had none (or had und), counted only when the write actually happened: a dry run, a disabled switch or a detector that could not decide all leave it at 0. Collapsed to one per file on purpose — a file with three tags is one file edited, and that is the question the line answers. It belongs on the status row because the row otherwise reports only what entered the library, never that the library itself was rewritten.

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.StatusStatsEntity.LooseSubtitlesRenamed
member.summary: F-M313: LOOSE subtitle files renamed so their NAME carries the detected language (F-M278). A separate counter from the one above because it is a different act on a different kind of file: a container gets a language tag INSIDE, a loose .srt gets a new name. Counted only on a real move — a refusal (target taken, unlistable directory, filesystem error) and a dry run leave both the file and the counter untouched.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.WorkerRunEntity
member.summary:
The LAST run of one worker (scheduled task), one row per worker.
Deliberately not a run HISTORY: the key is the worker's own task key, so a new run overwrites the previous row and the area can never grow. A history would need a retention policy and a prune path; the question this answers — "when did each worker last run, and how did it end?" — needs exactly one row per worker.
Stored in the DATA FILE rather than in memory: the previous status lived in static fields, so a Jellyfin restart reset it to "never run" and the GUI claimed a task had never executed minutes after it had (measured 30.09.2026). A database row survives a restart and is wiped by a database reset, which is the honest scope for it.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.PackEntity
member.summary:
F-M390 (operator order 02.11.2026): one row per season pack this plugin published, keyed by the season it covers — "<imdb>|S<season>|<lang>|<hi|plain>".
WHY IT EXISTS: a pack could only ever be built while every episode of the season was still in the run's upload queue. Once the episodes had gone up individually the season could never become a pack again, because nothing persisted the fact that it had been attempted — a later run would either repeat the same pack forever or never try again. The row is that fact: it says which season, in which language and variant, was packed, under which release, with which members, and which single uploads it absorbed.
The absorbed ids are kept deliberately. Folding singles into a pack means deleting them from SubDL, and a deletion with no record is a deletion nobody can audit or undo; with the ids on the row the plugin can name what it removed and put it back when a pack upload fails after them.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubdlDbContext
member.summary:
Central data context for Sub Scribe. One SQLite file, five clearly separated areas:
0 — file compatibility (schema/plugin/Jellyfin version)
1 — OSHash cache (path → file hash, disposable)
2 — video files, each with its embedded subtitle tracks beneath it
3 — sidecar .srt files, keyed by content
4 — burned download candidates
5 — cumulative GUI counters (one row)
Every area is keyed by a business key carried in the document's own Id field, never by an auto-assigned id. That is the correction of F-M194: with an auto id, an upsert of a "new" row can never find the row it means to update, which is what silently produced duplicates. It cannot happen now because the key is computed, not assigned.
Why SQLite through Entity Framework Core rather than the document store this replaced: Jellyfin already ships Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite and its native libe_sqlite3, and its PluginLoadContext resolves an assembly the plugin does not carry from the host. With ExcludeAssets=runtime on that package NOTHING rides along in the ZIP, where the previous engine had to ship its whole 510 KB engine. The provider's own service set (connection pooling, change tracking, migrations surface, VACUUM) is part of what the host already pays for.
The store is a file of this plugin's own, never Jellyfin's jellyfin.db. Jellyfin offers plugins no database interface at all, and its own schema is rebuilt by its migrations; a plugin writing there would lose data on a server update.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubdlDbContext.EnsurePacksTable
member.summary:
F-M390: creates the packs table on a data file that predates it.
EnsureCreated only builds a schema when the FILE is new, so a store written by an earlier build keeps its old tables and every query against the new one would throw. The statement is IF NOT EXISTS, so a fresh file (where EnsureCreated already built the table) and a second start are both no-ops; a failure is logged and swallowed, because a missing pack table must not stop the plugin from starting.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubdlDbContext.EnsureReportColumns
member.summary:
F-M450: adds the report columns to rejected_candidates on a data file that predates them.
EnsureCreated builds a schema only when the FILE is new and never alters an existing table, so an upgraded installation would otherwise keep five columns while every write names ten — and the failure would land in the middle of a download run. Each ALTER is guarded by the table's own column list, because SQLite has no "ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS". A failure is logged and swallowed: reporting must never stop the plugin from starting.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubdlDbContext.EnsurePackColumns
member.summary: F-M466: adds the pack fingerprint column. A table that already carries it is left alone, so the pass runs on every start and costs one PRAGMA.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubdlDbContext.EnsureStatusColumns
member.summary: F-M455: adds the status row's own late column — the count of broken subtitles reported to SubDL. A table that already carries it is left alone, so the pass runs on every start and costs one PRAGMA.

Records the running plugin and Jellyfin versions in area 0.
Called once at startup. Deliberately NOT called per run: writing the plugin's own version on every cycle would turn the audit record into a write amplifier.
member.param: Version of the hosting Jellyfin server.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubdlDbContext.ReadJournalMode
member.summary: Reads the journal mode the data file is actually in, through the live context.
member.returns: The mode string, e.g. wal or delete.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubdlDbContext.ClearPoolFor(System.String)
member.summary:
Drops every idle pooled connection for this database, so a file-level REPLACEMENT of the database is actually seen by the next open.
Called by the reset and restore paths immediately before they copy a file over the database. Pooling is off in this context, but SQLite keeps a process-wide pool registry and the plugin shares one path across several contexts over its lifetime — so the call is cheap insurance for the one operation that cannot tolerate a stale handle.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubdlDbContext.Checkpoint
member.summary:
Folds the write-ahead log into the main file, so the file on disk is a complete, self-contained snapshot.
Required before any file-level copy of the database. In WAL mode every committed write sits in <name>-wal until a checkpoint; a copy taken without this one carries the main file alone and silently loses everything written since the last checkpoint — and a RESTORE from such a copy leaves a stale -wal beside the restored file, which SQLite then tries to apply as if it belonged to it. The previous engine was a single file and needed none of this, which is exactly why the copy sites are worth checking when the format changes.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubdlDbContext.Prune(System.Nullable{System.DateTime})
member.summary: Delete all expired counters and very old runs.

members.member:
Physically compacts the data file. SQLite's VACUUM does in one statement what the previous engine needed a rebuild for: it rewrites the database into a dense file, which releases the pages that deletes freed.
Why this exists: deleting rows in SQLite does not shrink the file. The freed pages go on the freelist and the file stays as large as before the prune, so a state prune would leave the store physically untouched.
VACUUM cannot run inside a transaction, and this runs on a database other writers hold open — so the outcome is reported rather than assumed. The returned flag is true only when the database answers afterwards, so a failed compaction costs the size reduction and nothing else.
Compaction result: sizes before/after, collections rebuilt, and what became of the rebuild. F-M214: a database refresh compacts in the same run; measured over the database file plus its write-ahead log, because reporting the main file alone understates the starting size.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubdlDbContext.VerifyAndRepair(System.Exception)
member.summary:
Proves the database still answers after a failed compaction.
The probe is a real query — reading one row — because a flag would only restate what we already know about the exception. A SQLite connection that survives a failed VACUUM needs no repair; the check exists so the caller can tell "usable but not shrunk" from "broken".
member.param: The exception the compaction threw, for the log line.
member.returns: True when the database answers again.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubdlDbContext.MeasureFootprint
member.summary: Returns the byte sizes of the database file and its write-ahead log. SQLite in WAL mode keeps every delete and update in the side -wal file until a checkpoint folds it in.
member.returns: Main file size and WAL size in bytes; 0 for a file that does not exist.
