member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming
member.summary:
F-M239: the ONE reader of a sidecar file name.
Three places used to parse the same names with their own copy of the rules — the uploader (which knows the sdh/hi marker), the download pipeline's missing-language check, and the database refresh's on-disk check (neither of which knew it). The copies disagreed, and the disagreement was not cosmetic: MapToSubdl("sdh") falls back to the first two letters of an unknown tag, so the refresh read Movie.de.sdh.srt as the language "SD" — a language that does not exist — while DE looked absent. It then dropped the download mark as stale and the file was refetched on the next run, every run.
The marker is the whole point of the disagreement: sdh/hi name a VARIANT of a language, never a language. They are consumed as a marker and the real language token is read from the position before them.

member.name: F:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.CorrectedSlotMax
member.summary:
Highest slot a CORRECTED sidecar may take.
F-M315 (operator order 12.1.12.267): the slots above are RESERVED for the unsynchronized originals a correction keeps beside its result, so the writer of corrected files must stop below them. Without the cap the next corrected file of a language whose slots 1–49 are taken would be handed a name the original already uses, and the correction would overwrite the very file it exists to preserve.

member.name: F:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.OriginalSlotMin
member.summary:
Lowest and highest slot of the reserved ORIGINAL block.
F-M315: an original is assigned from UPWARD, which is what the operator asked for ("bei 1 und 50 anfangen zu zählen"): corrected files count up from 1, originals count up above them. Both blocks grow in the direction a viewer reads the track list, and the reserved number on each original tells the two kinds apart without opening anything.
member.remarks: Operator order 02.11.2026 ("unkorrigiert bitte ab 51 nummerieren"): the block starts at 51, so slot 50 is no longer handed out. Names already on disk keep their number — the planner only hands out FREE slots, so an existing .50.srt is read, listed and never overwritten.

member.name: F:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.OriginalSlotMax
member.summary: Highest slot of the reserved original block.

member.summary:
The slot number a sidecar name carries, or 0 when it carries none.
The reader's counterpart to : same shape, same two-digit slot, and the same rule that a slot sits LAST and the markers come before the language token. A name written before F-M316 (one digit, or no slot at all) returns 0 — it belongs to neither block and is therefore never mistaken for a reserved original.
member.returns: The slot, or 0.

member.summary:
True when a slot belongs to the reserved ORIGINAL block (51–99).
F-M315: the reservation is a property of the number, not of a file's content, so it is a pure function of the one datum the name carries. Nothing downstream has to hold state to tell an original from a corrected file.
member.returns: True when the slot is reserved for an unsynchronized original.

member.summary:
Builds the file name a sidecar gets next to the media file.
F-M260: the writer's counterpart to , in the SAME class on purpose. The downloader used to compose these names inline (ExternalName, plus two hand-written .sdh.srt concatenations), while and read them back — four places with the same idea of a name and no shared definition. That is how the earlier disagreement arose: MapToSubdl("sdh") read a hearing-impaired sidecar as the language "SD". Composing here, where parsing lives, means a name the writer produces is one the reader recognizes by construction.
member.param: Media file path (supplies directory and base name).
member.returns: Full path of the sidecar.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.PlanTarget(System.String,System.String,System.Boolean,System.Collections.Generic.ISet{System.String},System.Boolean)
member.summary:
The name a sidecar should carry once its language is known, lowest free slot first.
F-M278 (user decision 01.10.2026): a subtitle file whose NAME says nothing is renamed to the shape this plugin itself writes, because the name is the only thing Jellyfin, MediaElch and every reader in this codebase can see. An unlabelled <container>.srt is recognized by as "no language", so it is skipped by , never recorded as a fact, and the item is searched for a language its own disk already holds.
Slot 1 is the first name (F-M316: written as .01). A higher slot is chosen when that combination is already on disk — two unlabelled files detected as the same language are two entries, and a rename that overwrote one with the other would destroy a subtitle to tidy a file name. The rule is pure: the caller hands in the names that exist, so it can be asserted with plain strings.
member.param: The language, already resolved (by name token or by detection).
True when the file is the variant.
File names already present in the directory, as 's caller sees them.
member.returns: Full path of the name to move the file to. May already exist when every slot is taken.

member.summary:
The name an unsynchronized ORIGINAL gets beside the corrected file it was kept from.
F-M315 (operator order 07.10.2026): the original is a normal sidecar — same language, same hearing-impaired flag, no marker of its own — that differs only in the SLOT it occupies. It is numbered from UPWARD and takes the first free number, so up to fifty originals of one language can sit beside one media file. Jellyfin lists each as its own selectable track titled with that number, which is what lets the operator pick the untouched version in the player.
It is deliberately NOT marked forced: a forced subtitle is a different thing in this codebase (it carries only foreign-language scenes and is never delivered) and the flag would make the file read as something it is not.
There is no "already exists, overwrite anyway" fallback here. When all ten reserved slots are taken the caller's own existence check refuses the write — fifty uncorrected versions of one language beside one media file is not a case to invent a name for.
member.param: The language of the corrected file the original belongs to.
True when the corrected file is the variant.
File names already present in the directory.
member.returns: Full path for the original, or null when every reserved slot is taken.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.IsHearingImpairedToken(System.String)
member.summary:
True when a name token marks a hearing-impaired variant rather than a language.
Only sdh qualifies. The earlier rule also accepted hi, which is wrong on two counts: hi is the ISO 639-1 code for Hindi — the mapper maps hin to HI, so a real Hindi subtitle named Movie.hi.srt was read as a hearing-impaired marker and, because no language token preceded it, dropped entirely. And nothing in this plugin ever writes .hi.srt: the downloader writes .sdh.srt, and Hindi sidecars are written .hi.srt by every other tool. The marker is sdh only.
member.returns: True when the token is a hearing-impaired marker.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.IsForcedToken(System.String)
member.summary:
True when a name token marks a FORCED track rather than a language.
F-M284 (user decision 02.10.2026): forced is the marker every other tool writes (Movie.de.forced.srt), so it is read like sdh is. It is not a marker the plugin writes itself: SubDL has no forced counterpart (measured live 02.10.2026 — no filter, no field, 0 of 22 candidates named forced), so nothing is ever downloaded as a forced sidecar. Recognizing it is what lets such a file be recorded as what it IS instead of being counted as the film's dialogue.
Strictly the whole token, for the same reason the HI marker is: a substring rule would read real names as markers and lose their language.
member.returns: True when the token is a forced marker.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.ReadFlags(System.String)
member.summary:
Reads the MARKERS (hearing-impaired, forced) out of a sidecar name, without resolving a language and without needing the media base name.
F-M284: extracted so the two callers that need only the flags — the sidecar backfill, which holds a stored file name rather than a directory to walk, and — cannot disagree about what a marker is. The scan starts at the END and skips the numbered slot first, because that is where the writer puts it (<base>.<lang>.sdh.02.srt).
member.returns: The two flags the name states.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.Parse(System.String,System.String)
member.summary:
Reads the language and BOTH properties (hearing-impaired, forced) out of a sidecar file name.
Recognized shapes, all relative to the media base name: <base>.srt (no language in the name), <base>.<lang>.srt, <base>.<lang>.sdh.srt / <base>.<lang>.hi.srt, <base>.<lang>.forced.srt, the two markers combined (<base>.<lang>.sdh.forced.srt, either order), and the numbered slots, which F-M316 makes two digits and always present (<base>.<lang>.01.srt … .99.srt; a one-digit or absent slot written before F-M316 still reads back).
The language token itself keeps the permissive resolution it always had (two letters direct, three letters through the ISO 639-2 map, unknown three-letter tags falling back to their first two letters). Only the marker case is strict — that fallback is precisely what must not see a marker.
member.returns: Language (null when the name carries none) with both flags; null when the name is not a sidecar at all.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.List(System.String)
member.summary:
The sidecar files next to a media file, in one directory listing.
Callers need different projections of the same fact — the uploader wants paths, the existence checks want just the languages, the coverage reader wants the DATA (language plus both flags) — so the listing is done once here and projected by the callers, rather than each caller walking the directory with its own idea of what a file name means. F-M284: the tuple carries forced as well, because a `.forced.srt` is not the film's dialogue and must not be counted as coverage.
member.returns: One entry per recognized sidecar.

member.returns: Language → (any file present, hearing-impaired file present).

member.summary: Which of the wanted languages have no sidecar on disk.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.PresentPairs(System.String)
member.summary:
F-M282 (user decision 02.10.2026): the pairs that have file evidence next to the media file.
This replaces PresentTokens and with it the whole string-token vocabulary (HiTokenSuffix, IsHiToken, TokenLanguage). Those existed to carry a hearing-impaired property through a comma-separated language list — and every helper that mapped a token back to its plain language was a place the conflation re-entered, because a language-keyed reader then re-requested the LANGUAGE for a missing variant and fetched the regular subtitle over the file already on disk.
A pair cannot be projected back by accident: there is no spelling of DE that carries the variant and no parse that can lose it. The rule of the old reader is kept: a subtitle of language L proves L whether or not it is the variant, and proves L (HI) only when it IS.
member.returns: Pairs with file evidence.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.IsDialogueStream(MediaBrowser.Model.Entities.MediaStream)
member.summary:
True when this stream is a subtitle track that carries the film's DIALOGUE — readable text, not forced.
F-M284 (user decision 02.10.2026): this is the ONE predicate behind every "is this track part of the film?" decision in the plugin. A forced track carries the lines of foreign-language scenes only (F-M246), so it is not dialogue and must not count as coverage, must not be uploaded, and needs no language tag. A bitmap track carries pixels (F-M6/F-M257), so it cannot be read at all.
It exists as a named rule because the same judgement used to be re-derived from Jellyfin's flags in five separate call sites (the seeder twice, the upload pipeline, the language gate, and the embedded-presence check). Copies drift: the four name parsers this codebase used to carry are the standing proof, and one of them silently read .sdh as the language "SD". A caller that needs a different QUESTION asks a different predicate; a caller that needs the same question calls this one.
member.returns: True when the stream is a non-forced text subtitle track.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.IsHearingImpairedStream(MediaBrowser.Model.Entities.MediaStream)
member.summary:
F-M71's HI detection on an embedded stream, in ONE place. Jellyfin's own flag first, then the title. The uploader and the downloader each carried a copy of this; the uploader's copy never asked the flag, so a file whose HI stream was flagged but not titled read as two different things depending on which side asked.
F-M254: cc joins the markers. Closed captions and SDH describe the same audience — the captions carry the non-dialogue cues ([ BEEPING ], [ GRUNTING ], musical notes) that separate them from a plain subtitle — but only "SDH" was recognized. Files titled CC therefore wrote false into the registry, so the HI variant read as absent and the language was fetched again although the variant was already in the container. The marker is matched on a word boundary and not as a substring on purpose: cc sits inside real language names (Occitan), and reading that as hearing-impaired would repeat the hi/Hindi mistake this method's sibling documents.
member.returns: True when the stream is a hearing-impaired subtitle track.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.IsForcedStream(MediaBrowser.Model.Entities.MediaStream)
member.summary:
F-M246: True when the stream is a FORCED subtitle track.
A forced track carries only the lines of foreign-language scenes, not the film's dialogue. It therefore never counts as a subtitle of the film — neither as coverage on the download side (where it must not mark a language present) nor as upload work (where there is nothing worth publishing: the same few lines, usually one cue).
One predicate for both directions, so neither can drift. A hearing-impaired track is NOT affected: SDH is the same dialogue with annotations.
F-M367 (26.10.2026): the FLAG alone is not enough — the TITLE is the second source, as already reads it, because a muxer may leave DISPOSITION:forced at 0 on a track titled Forced. Word boundary, so enforced is no marker.
member.returns: True when the stream is a forced subtitle track.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.ResolveToken(System.String)
member.summary: Language token → SubDL code: two letters direct, three through the mapper.
member.returns: SubDL language code, or null.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.EmbeddedPresentLanguages(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{MediaBrowser.Model.Entities.MediaStream})
member.summary:
F-M246: the languages an embedded subtitle track makes "present", in ONE place.
The download pipeline's missing-language check and the seeder's queueing gate each walked the subtitle streams with their own copy of this loop, and neither ever asked MediaStream.IsForced. A forced track carries only the lines of foreign-language scenes — it is not a subtitle of the film — yet it counted as full coverage for its language, so a file whose English existed only as a forced track was reported as settled and never received a real English subtitle. Measured on the 28.09.2026 library: 4 items whose English is forced-only (Taylor Swift — The Eras Tour, no sidecar), plus 8 whose Hindi is, all already marked "all target languages settled".
Only TEXT subtitle streams count. A bitmap track (dvdsub, pgssub) carries painted pixels — there is nothing to read, nothing to extract and nothing to publish, so it is not coverage for its language (user decision 30.09.2026: "Bild sub ist nicht da"). Measured on the 30.09.2026 library: 86 items carry a target language ONLY as a bitmap track (`dvdsub`/`pgssub`, e.g. the "480p DVD x265 Panda" films and `Person Of Interest S02`), and every one of them was counted as covered, so no subtitle was ever fetched for them.
A hearing-impaired track DOES count: it is the same film's dialogue, just annotated. So the rule is "any non-forced TEXT subtitle stream", and the HI switch is answered separately from the registry (F-M254) rather than from the stream list.
One copy only, for the same reason the name parse has one: the two callers must give the same answer, and the seeder's answer decides whether the pipeline ever sees the item.
member.param: Media streams of the item (may be null when unavailable).
member.returns: Language codes carried by a non-forced embedded subtitle track.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.EmbeddedTracks(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{MediaBrowser.Model.Entities.MediaStream})
member.summary:
F-M257: the embedded tracks of a file as (position, language, HI) triples — the ONE reader for callers that record or compare individual tracks rather than just their languages.
The position is the index into the UNFILTERED subtitle list, because ffmpeg's 0:s:N counts bitmap and forced tracks as well; a position taken from a filtered list names a different stream. Forced tracks are left out for the same reason the presence check leaves them out (F-M246) — a forced track carries the lines of foreign-language scenes, not the film's dialogue.
Only TEXT subtitle streams are returned, exactly as the uploader selects them. A bitmap track (dvdsub, pgssub) carries painted pixels: it cannot be extracted, so it can never be uploaded, and it is not a subtitle the reader can use either (user decision 30.09.2026: "Bild sub ist nicht da"). Recording it would claim a coverage that does not exist for either direction.
Untagged streams are left out too: a language that cannot be mapped has no side in the registry, and inventing one was the phantom-language defect F-M239 removed.
One copy only, shared by the seeder's observation write and any pipeline-side comparison, so the two cannot drift the way the four name parsers and the three HI readers did.
member.param: All subtitle streams of the item, UNFILTERED (as Jellyfin returns them).
member.returns: One triple per mappable, non-forced, TEXT embedded subtitle track.
member.summary:
F-M284 (user decision 02.10.2026): the embedded subtitle tracks of a file, with BOTH properties, observed rather than filtered.
This used to skip forced and bitmap streams outright, which meant the registry never held a row for a track that exists — and then every caller that cared re-derived the exclusion from Jellyfin's stream flag, in five separate places (the seeder twice, the upload pipeline, the language gate, and the coverage check). A fact that is never recorded is a fact that gets re-guessed: the rule now lives in ONE reader, and the row states what the file carries.
Bitmap tracks are still EXCLUDED, and that is a different matter: they carry no text at all (F-M6), so there is no subtitle datum to record — no language to resolve, nothing to upload, nothing to hash.
A forced track is recorded with Forced = true and deliberately still carries its language: that is the whole point of recording it. It does not count as coverage anywhere (a forced track is not the film's dialogue, F-M246), so the language stays open and is searched for — and because the row exists, the reason is visible instead of having to be re-derived.
member.returns: One triple per mappable, non-bitmap TEXT embedded subtitle track.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SidecarNaming.SubtitlePositions(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{MediaBrowser.Model.Entities.MediaStream})
member.summary:
F-M258: the stream positions the item HAS, whether or not their language is readable.
reports only tracks whose language resolves, so a track whose tag Jellyfin cannot read yet — notably right after the language gate wrote it, because Jellyfin caches its stream list — is absent from that list even though it exists. A caller comparing stored rows against it would read "the language is unknown" as "the track is gone" and drop a valid row. This answers the other half of the question: does the position still exist at all? Positions follow the same rule as — the unfiltered, non-external subtitle list, because ffmpeg's 0:s:N counts every subtitle stream including forced and bitmap ones.
member.returns: Positions of every non-external subtitle stream.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SubtitleCoverage
member.summary:
Which subtitle DATA are covered for one media file — the ONE answer every reader asks.
F-M283 (user decision 02.10.2026): "is this item done?" is no longer a stored verdict. The download mark (SubtitlesDownloadedAt plus a comma-separated language list) was a SECOND truth beside the rows that actually describe the subtitles, and the two drifted:
the short-circuit asked the disk PLUS the stored variant verdict, while the check that decided whether to WRITE the mark asked the disk alone — so a variant embedded in the container had a registry verdict and no sidecar, the withhold check reported "no file evidence" and refused the mark, and the mark was then never written, the item stayed due, and every pass re-downloaded the regular subtitle again;
a language-keyed mark let one file stand in for another: a successful regular save closed the variant's slot although no variant file existed.
With the mark gone there is nothing left to drift. Completeness is DERIVED, on every ask, from the evidence that describes the subtitles themselves — and because it is derived it cannot be overtaken by a deletion: removing Movie.de.sdh.srt removes its evidence, and the item is due again with no invalidation step and no bookkeeping.
The evidence is read at the grain of , from three sources, and all three are consulted for every caller so that two readers of one question can never disagree again:
the files next to the media file — the exact pair each sidecar name states. This is what self-corrects, and it is why a deleted variant makes the item due;
the embedded rows of the container — a track inside the file, with its own language and its own hearing-impaired flag, written by whichever pass observed the streams (F-M257). This is the source that used to be missing on the withhold side;
the language-level embedded evidence a caller may hold (Jellyfin's stream list, when the configuration counts embedded tracks as coverage). It speaks about a language, never about a variant.
The language rule is kept from the previous reader: a subtitle of language L proves L, whether or not it is the hearing-impaired variant (SDH is the same dialogue with annotations, F-M243), and it proves L (HI) only when it IS that variant. So a lone Movie.de.sdh.srt satisfies both pairs of German, and a lone Movie.de.srt satisfies German only.
No verdict is made here about whether a datum SHOULD exist: the caller supplies the pairs it requires. The coverage question is "is there evidence", and the caller combines it with the QA budget to decide what to search for.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SubtitlePresence
member.summary:
F-M234: what subtitle files are actually present on disk for a media file.
This exists because two different questions were being answered by one flag. "Is this item finished?" is a stored verdict; "is this subtitle still there?" is a fact about the filesystem. Only the second one can be re-checked, and it is the only thing that can prove a stored verdict wrong — a deleted sidecar leaves the verdict intact and the item silently done forever.
F-M239: the NAME rules moved to — the copy that used to live here did not know the "sdh" marker and read Movie.de.sdh.srt as the phantom language "SD", which made the refresh declare valid download marks stale. What stays in this class is the ROOT gate: answers "may I trust a verdict of absent at all?", which is a question about directories, not about file names.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SubtitlePresence.RootsUsable(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyCollection{System.String})
member.summary:
F-M234 (C), fail-safe: true when every root exists and lists cleanly.
The same two-tier rule the oshash cache uses. An unmounted volume reports every path as missing; forgetting verdicts on that basis would destroy valid state, so a single unusable root means the caller must skip its deletions entirely. "Unknown" is never "deleted".
member.returns: True when every root exists and can be listed.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.SubtitleRef
member.summary:
One subtitle DATUM: a language plus the properties OF THAT DATUM — hearing-impaired and forced.
This is the atom the whole plugin judges. A hearing-impaired subtitle is not a property of the media file and not a modifier of a language — it is its own subtitle, with its own identity, its own row and its own hash. Movie.de.srt and Movie.de.sdh.srt are two files, two sidecar rows keyed by their content, and two entries in the embedded area when they sit in the container. The tuple (language, hearing-impaired, forced) is therefore the smallest thing a question can be asked about, and every reader and writer in the plugin asks at that grain.
F-M282 (user decision 02.10.2026): the tuple replaces the string token vocabulary. The download mark used to carry DE and DE:hi as text inside a comma-separated language list, which meant the properties had to be re-derived — and every projection that mapped a token back to its plain language was a place the conflation re-entered: a missing variant re-requested the LANGUAGE, so the regular subtitle was fetched over the file already on disk (41 downloads in one run against a 50/day limit, 35 marks withheld in the same run, the same content hash on three consecutive days). A structured tuple cannot be projected back by accident: there is no spelling of "DE" that carries the variant, and no parse that can lose it.
F-M284 (user decision 02.10.2026): the two properties are NOT symmetric, and the type says so. Jellyfin reports both on its streams, so both are readable at the source — but only hearing-impaired has a counterpart on SubDL's side:
hearing-impaired is bilateral. SubDL serves it from two separate server-side pools (&hi=1 / &hi=0, F-M241) and accepts the flag on upload, so the datum can be SEARCHED for and DELIVERED.
forced is local. SubDL has no forced filter and returns no forced field — measured live 02.10.2026: forced=1, forced=0 and no parameter all returned the same 10 candidates, the response carries only hi, and 0 of 22 candidates across three languages carried "forced" in the release name. A forced subtitle therefore cannot be sought, fetched or announced; it can only be observed.
The consequence is the rule the datum carries: never counts as coverage. A language whose only track is forced is NOT covered — a forced track carries only the lines of foreign-language scenes, not the film's dialogue (F-M246) — so the regular datum stays open and is searched for. Before this type existed that rule was re-derived in five separate call sites; it now lives in one reader.
The type is a value: two tuples with the same language and the same flags ARE the same datum, so sets and dictionaries of them answer "do I already have this file" without a comparison helper. The language is normalized on construction, which is what makes that equality hold across the case differences the sources produce (Jellyfin writes eng, the configuration EN).

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.WorkerOffState
member.summary:
F-M352 (operator order 19.10.2026): decides whether a worker is switched OFF — the note under the Workers list says "off" for it (operator: the lamps stay as they are, the off state is noted in the worker section as the last entry).
The conditions are not invented here — each one is a hard refusal that already exists in the code, so the lamp states what the run would actually do:
Download: DownloadEnabled false (SubdlDownloadTask), empty SelectedLibraries (F-M213, hard stop for both directions), an empty target-language list (DownloadPipeline "No target languages configured"), or a missing credential (DownloadPipeline/MissingCredentials).
Upload: UploadEnabled false (SubdlUploadTask), empty SelectedLibraries, or a missing credential. The upload has no language list, so it has no language condition.
Upload postprocessing: UploadEnabled false or the cadence on Never/Manual/OnArrival — exactly the gate the scheduler uses before it arms the anchor (F-M291). The library selection is deliberately NOT a condition: the postprocessing reads /user/mySubtitles and never touches the library, so libraries do not stop it.
The lamps and every stored outcome are left untouched: this class only feeds the trailing "off" notes, so no run is ever hidden by a switch (operator finding: a greyed row made a just-started manual postprocessing run read "off").

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.WorkerRunRegistry
member.summary:
Records the LAST run of each worker (scheduled task) in the data file, so the configuration page can answer "when did the download worker last run, and how did it end?" without reading logs.
One row per worker, keyed by the worker's own task key: a new run OVERWRITES that row, so the area never grows and needs no retention policy. This is deliberately not a run history — a history would need a prune path and a cap, and the question does not ask for one.
Why the database and not a static field: the postprocessing status used to live in UploadPipeline statics, so every Jellyfin restart reset it to "never run" and the status endpoint reported a worker as never-executed minutes after it had run (measured 30.09.2026). A database row survives a restart, and a database reset wipes it — which is exactly the honest scope for a progress record.
A worker has exactly ONE row, so the write path is an upsert and must never be a history insert. Every worker is expected to appear in the GUI even before its first run, so merges the stored rows with the known workers instead of returning only what was written.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.WorkerRunRegistry.DescribeCycle(System.Boolean,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary:
The status a worker reports for the cycle it took part in.
Colour criteria (user-approved 30.09.2026), one principle for every worker: GREEN = the work really ran and ended without an exception; YELLOW = the work did not happen but nothing is broken (quota, run-lock deferral, user stop); RED = something is broken (exception, failed cycle, unreachable core); GREY = deliberately not run (disabled), never run, or a scan that found nothing to do.
Why the direction's and the seeder's fate are both inputs: the download/upload tasks do no work of their own, they start the cycle and wait. Reporting their own "ok" was wrong twice over — it claimed success when the 30-minute wait cap expired while the seeder was STILL scanning (measured 30.09.2026: cycle start 16:16, seeder scanned until 17:12, GUI said "ok"), and it hid a quota stop (same day 18:51: "Daily download limit (429)", 2 of 1144 items, GUI said "ok").
member.param: False when the wait hit its cap and the cycle is still working.
The seeder's fate in THIS cycle, or null when it reported none.
The matching seeder detail; ranked in the red/yellow/grey branches only.
This direction's fate (download/upload) in the cycle, or empty/null when it ran without a special fate.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.AnchorJobGate
member.summary:
F-M368 (28.10.2026): the two decisions every diced-anchor job needs, as PURE functions — testable without a server, a clock or a task manager.
Why this exists: the anchor blocks spelled both decisions inline, and the second one inside the first — due = … && (marker != today || now < until) with if (due && now >= until). The two clauses exclude each other: while the deadline lies in the future the fire gate blocks, and the moment it arrives the due-term falls to false, because the earlier fire already consumed the day marker. A run that had deferred itself on a busy lock therefore never came back. Measured 28.10.2026 16:25: "Database refresh re-fire scheduled at 15:40 UTC", followed by not one refresh line for the rest of the day — the row stayed yellow at 16:24 for the rest of the evening.
And the deadline was written in TWO clock kinds: the anchor blocks with DateTime.Now, the tasks with DateTime.UtcNow, while every comparison used DateTime.Now. In CET a UTC-stamped deadline reads one hour in the past, in CEST two. Hence the split signature: for deadlines, for anchors.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlDatabaseRefreshTask
member.summary:
The database refresh: reconciles the stored state with reality.
F-M94 (user decision 11.09.2026) started this as a prune: drop tracker state whose Jellyfin item no longer exists, because a deleted movie left its retry/quota memories behind forever.
F-M234 (user decision 28.09.2026) widened it into a refresh. Deleting an item is only the crudest way reality drifts from the database: a subtitle file can be deleted while its media item stays, a download mark can claim "complete" for a language whose file is gone, and a sidecar can vanish without anything else changing. Those cases were invisible — the stored verdicts stayed, so the item was reported complete forever and only a file-system probe in the running pipeline could ever notice. The refresh now verifies the FILE side of each verdict, not only the item side.
FAIL-SAFE SEMANTICS (user requirement: "what happens when no access exists right now?"): - "Unknown ≠ deleted": when the library manager or the filesystem is not reliably queryable, the ENTIRE run deletes NOTHING. A missed refresh costs nothing; a false one would erase valid retry/quota memories and live subtitle verdicts. - Existence checks: LibraryManager.GetItemById → null counts as dead ONLY after a positive probe proved the library responds (a live item resolves). - File paths (oshash cache, subtitles) are only dropped when the file is gone AND its parent directory still exists and lists cleanly — an offline/unmounted volume reports everything as missing and must not nuke valid state (two-tier rule, now shared in SubtitlePresence). - No TTL/age-based pruning here by design (decided 11.09.2026): age proves nothing about item existence; the existence checks above are the truth source.

Builds the detail line the configuration page shows for a database refresh.
Static and pure so the wording is testable without a Jellyfin host.
A compaction that fell back to the rebuild is appended to the line (user decision 30.09.2026: the compaction failure itself will NOT be solved, the rebuild is the accepted answer — but the row said "ok" with a line that read like a clean run, so the fallback was invisible). This is a NOTE, not a red light: the refresh did its work and the store came back usable.
member.param: The exception that aborted the refresh, or null.
How many pieces of dead state were removed in total.
How many dead-state rows were removed.
How many vanished subtitle verdicts were forgotten.
How many stale embedded rows were forgotten.
How many items still have a required file missing.
A note about the compaction step, or empty when it compacted cleanly.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlDatabaseRefreshTask.BackfillForcedFlags(Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubdlDbContext)
member.summary:
F-M284 (user decision 02.10.2026): backfills the FORCED property on rows written before it existed.
A document store has no schema, so a row written by an older build simply has no Forced field and reads back as false. That is not a harmless default here: a forced track would then be indistinguishable from the film's dialogue, so it would COUNT AS COVERAGE — the language would look settled although its only track carries foreign-language scenes, and the regular subtitle would never be fetched. The stored rows are the state, so they are brought up to date rather than left to look settled.
The flag is read back off the row's own name, which is where it came from in the first place: a sidecar states its markers in its file name (Movie.de.forced.srt), so the backfill derives nothing new — it re-reads a fact the name always carried.
An EMBEDDED row cannot be backfilled this way and is deliberately left alone: its flag lives in the container's stream list, not in a name, and the next scan or download pass observes the track again and writes the current value. Guessing false there would be the very mistake this method exists to undo.
member.param: Content registry (accepts the sidecar rows directly).
member.returns: Number of sidecar rows whose forced flag was set.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlDatabaseRefreshTask.ForgetStaleEmbeds(Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.ContentHashRegistry,System.Collections.Generic.HashSet{System.String})
member.summary:
F-M258: drops embedded rows that no longer match the file's own tracks.
The sidecar half of this lives in and needs only File.Exists. An embedded track has no file, so its evidence is the stream list — this is the only caller that can read it, which is why the check lives here.
Fail-safe, the same rule the rest of the refresh follows ("unknown ≠ deleted"): an item Jellyfin no longer resolves, a file that is gone, or a stream list that comes back empty is skipped rather than judged. An empty list is the dangerous case — an item Jellyfin cannot probe returns no streams, and treating that as "the file has no tracks" would delete every row of a library that is merely offline. Only a NON-empty list that disagrees with a stored row is evidence.
member.param: Item ids still present in Jellyfin.
member.returns: Number of removed embedded rows.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlDatabaseRefreshTask.CountItemsWithOpenFiles(Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubdlDbContext,Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.ContentHashRegistry,System.Collections.Generic.HashSet{System.String})
member.summary:
F-M283 (user decision 02.10.2026): how many items have an OPEN required file.
This used to be InvalidateStaleDownloadMarks: it walked every stored download mark, re-derived its "open tokens" and DROPPED the mark when a subtitle had vanished — a repair of a second truth that should never have existed. Measured on the live library, that machinery dropped 450 valid marks in one run on its first attempt (disk-only evidence against files whose subtitles sat inside the container) and, once narrowed, kept contradicting a mark the pipeline could not write at all: 35 marks withheld in a single run.
With the mark gone there is nothing to drop and nothing to repair. What remains is the question itself — "which required files are missing on this disk?" — asked through the SAME reader the pipeline and the seeder use (), so a deletion here and a deletion there cannot be judged differently. A vanished .sdh.srt is simply an open pair, and the item is due on the next run without any bookkeeping at all.
The method only REPORTS, deliberately: this is the refresh, and its job is to make the state visible. It writes nothing, so a run can never take work away from the pipeline.
member.param: Item ids still present in Jellyfin.
member.returns: Number of items with at least one open required file.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlDatabaseRefreshTask.EmbeddedLanguagesForCoverage(Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.SubdlDbContext,Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Registry.ContentHashRegistry,Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Data.MediaEntity)
member.summary:
F-M234: the embedded languages that count as coverage for a stored download mark.
Same sources the download pipeline consults, in the same order of authority: the REGISTRY first, because Jellyfin caches its stream list and still reports the OLD tag of a container corrected earlier in the cycle, then Jellyfin's own list as the second opinion.
Empty when the configuration does not count embedded tracks at all, and empty while the item cannot be probed. The caller then decides on the files alone, which is the pre-01.10.2026 behaviour — narrow, but never worse than the truth.
member.param: The media row whose mark is being judged.
member.returns: Languages carried by the file's own tracks.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlEventDispatcher
member.summary: (user decision 14.09.2026): the EXECUTION engine ("EventTrigger"). Three event sources feed one cycle machine: 1. Library change (ItemAdded) → on-arrival gates (F-M55) → arrival debounce (F-M1a) (NOT reset by further events, user decision 12.09.2026) → cycle scoped to the directions that want on-arrival. 2. Refetch tick (from the scheduler coordinator / scheduled tasks) → cycle. 3. Quota recovery fire → cycle (seed finds nothing → cheap no-op). Cycle = seed → downloader → uploader (sequenced per direction, user decision 13.09.2026) → new material during cycle? → repeat, else done. The WHEN belongs to the scheduler (SubdlSchedulerCoordinator): it owns due times, the lock probe and the spacing deferral; this class only decides HOW a run executes once triggered.

member.summary:
Asks SubDL whether the download direction has any allowance left, ONCE per cycle.
Operator order 08.10.2026: "Api limit oder download limit voll, downloader startet erst garnicht." Measured on prod the same day: the 50/day download limit had been spent since 05:59, yet four further cycles (20:45, 21:09, 21:32, 21:33) each walked ~1 000 of 1 144 queued items, spent the day's SEARCH allowance (59 → 194) and saved nothing — 104 s per cycle into the same wall.
The check lives HERE, not in the seeder: the seeder fills queues and does not decide policy, so it takes the answer as a plain flag exactly like config.DownloadEnabled. One read-only call to /me per cycle, which consumes no allowance (verified: the settings page queries it freely).
A failure to READ the counters is NOT a verdict — it returns null and the cycle proceeds as before. Fail-closed here would turn a network hiccup into a silent day without downloads, which is worse than one wasted run; the pipeline still guards itself.

member.summary:
F-M23: updates the persisted cumulative status counters from pipeline summaries.
Stored in the database since 25.09.2026 (was: plugin configuration XML). The XML sits next to user settings while the data being counted lives in the database, so a database reset used to leave the counters behind and the display drifted from the data (measured 25.09.2026: 311 uploaded rows in the database, 743 in the display). Writing them here keeps both in step.

F-M322 (operator order 08.10.2026): writes the auto-sync's own worker row for the download run.
The light answers ONE question — did the alignment work — and the operator asked for it as its own line, both in the Workers list and under the download switch. It uses the SAME status words and colours as every other worker (F-M268), so nothing new had to be invented for it:
GREEN (`ok`) — the run aligned at least one subtitle, or found every candidate it measured already in sync (F-M321). Both are the work DONE; the statistics counter, by the operator's own order, covers only the files that were really MOVED.
YELLOW/GREY (`skipped`) — the alignment is switched off, or the run measured nothing at all. Nothing was asked of it and nothing is broken.
RED (`failed`) — the run reported failures and aligned nothing.
A dry run reports skipped with its own note: a dry run writes no file, so it cannot have aligned anything, and a green light would claim a correction that exists nowhere (F-M247).
member.param: The download run's summary, or null when this direction is the UPLOAD: the auto-sync belongs to the download run, and an upload run holds no alignment result.

member.summary:
Whether THIS cycle already wrote the given direction's row itself (start and finish).
The waiting scheduled tasks and the arrival path both used to write these rows after the whole cycle, which is why a direction stayed blue while its SIBLING ran: the download leg ended, nobody finished its row, and the upload leg then lit a second lamp. A row written by the direction itself is complete and must not be overwritten with a cycle-level summary.
member.returns: True when this cycle already wrote that row.

member.summary:
Writes a direction's row from ITS OWN result, start to finish — the row states what this direction did and nothing else.
Operator order 08.10.2026 ("jeder worker meldet nur sich selbst"; "seeder gets blue only, download only download, upload only upload — as it is successive"). Called from 's finally, so it runs on the success path, on a failure and on a cancellation; a direction that had nothing to say (its queue was empty, so no run ever began) leaves the row to the waiting task exactly as before.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlEventDispatcher.MarkAutoSyncRunning(System.Boolean,Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.Configuration.PluginConfiguration)
member.summary:
F-M340 (operator finding 09.10.2026): "Ampel auto sync soll auf run springen". Opens the Auto-Sync row at the moment the DOWNLOAD run that will feed the alignment starts.
Only for the download, and only when the alignment can actually produce work: an upload run holds no audio fit at all, and with the switch off the row reports `skipped` from the summary path — opening it blue first would promise a run that never comes. Two conditions, because the light means "work is in flight NOW" and nothing else.
The row is opened with no detail: a start time that is real and an outcome that is honest, while the number of files this run will fit is unknown at this point. The detail arrives with the summary. `Finish` keeps the start stamp it finds, so the duration shown on the page is this run's real fit time in place of the fraction of a second the old placement produced.
member.param: Direction whose run is starting; only the download opens this row.
Live configuration — the alignment's own switch decides.

member.remarks: A row left on `run` after the run is over is worse than one that never lit: the operator reads a working alignment on a plugin that has stopped working on it. The summary path clears before it writes its own verdict, so this guard never overwrites a real result — the flag, not the outcome word, decides who writes.

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlOshashRefreshTask
member.summary: F-M119 (user decision 14.09.2026): OSHash refresh is a SCHEDULER job, not a lazy uploader concern. The coordinator fires this task on its own diced WEEKLY anchor (`RandomOshashTime`, "D HH:mm", drawn once at install, never re-rolled) — every week, with no nth-week gating: the prune's `IsoWeek` gate does not apply here. It walks the central oshash cache and recomputes every entry whose trust window (OshashRefresh cadence) has expired or whose size+mtime fingerprint changed. `OshashRefresh = Never` does NOT disable the job — it narrows it to fingerprint mismatches only (zero media reads in the steady state); the trust window is not a cadence. Missing files are left alone (the state prune owns deletions); the uploader keeps a lazy self-healing path for cache misses (a file it has never seen) but no longer revalidates aged entries itself. Holds the global pipeline run lock for the whole pass (registry mutation — same rationale as the prune, F-M94h).

member.name: T:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSchedulerCoordinator
member.summary: THE scheduler (F-M48 08.09.2026, 12.09.2026, 14.09.2026): one owner of all due times — refetch anchors (diced once per installation, persisted in plugin config), recovery fires (F-M65, persisted to recovery-fires.json since F-M116) and the weekly database refresh job. A 30-s tick fires due jobs THROUGH the global run lock: busy lock → the job defers by JobSpacingMinutes (config, default 15) and retries — nothing is dropped, nothing overlaps. A missed anchor slot IS caught up (F-M156): the slot fires on the first tick where it is past-due and unconsumed, and the persisted marker keeps it from stacking or replaying across a restart. Past-due recovery fires fire on the next tick. Jobs are queued via ITaskManager so they stay visible/manually triggerable in the dashboard; the event dispatcher executes them (see its header).

member.name: P:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSchedulerCoordinator.Instance
member.summary: F-M65: singleton reference — pipelines (built outside DI by PluginServiceRegistrator) reach the coordinator to schedule recovery fires without a constructor-injection detour. Set once by the DI singleton, cleared on dispose.

member.name: F:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSchedulerCoordinator.MaxRescheduleAttempts
member.summary: (user decision 25.09.2026: stop rescheduling at the limit): every reschedule of a slot (lock-busy defer, rate-limit spacing) is COUNTED. After (16) the rescheduling stops instead of silently pushing the same work forward forever. The slot's next REGULAR anchor picks the work up again — which is why giving up is a warning, not an error. Reset on a real fire, and at the daily roll-over (see ).

member.name: F:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSchedulerCoordinator._rescheduleBudgetDayUtc
member.summary: UTC day the reschedule budget was last reset for. The counters are per-day, so a slot that exhausted its budget today gets a fresh one tomorrow instead of staying blocked until a restart — the counter lives in RAM, so without this the limit was effectively "until the next process start" (measured 25.09.2026: a slot sat at 11 attempts with no path back, because the refusal drops its recovery fire and a Manual install has no regular anchor that could clear it).

members.member:
Counts one reschedule for a slot. Returns false when the attempt limit is exhausted — the caller must then NOT reschedule (the regular anchor owns the slot again).
Slot label: download, upload, postprocess, refresh, oshash, refetch. Why the reschedule happened (lock-busy, rate-limit, …) — log only. True when another reschedule is still allowed. F-M205: one counter per slot, cleared on a real fire and by the per-day budget reset (F-M208).

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSchedulerCoordinator.ResetReschedule(System.String)
member.summary: Clears the reschedule counter for a slot — called when the slot actually fired, i.e. the blockage cleared (user decision 25.09.2026).

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSchedulerCoordinator.ResetDailyRescheduleBudget
member.summary:
Clears the reschedule budget for every slot once the UTC day rolls over — the same boundary the SubDL quota reset uses. Called from the scheduler tick (so it also happens while nothing else is running) and from (so a trigger arriving right after midnight is never counted against yesterday's budget).
The counters are per-day on purpose: the limit exists to stop one slot from spinning inside a single day, not to block it across days. Without this the limit was unbounded in time, because a refused slot loses its recovery fire and cannot reach the on-fire reset.

member.name: F:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSchedulerCoordinator.CancelledDetail
member.summary:
F-M351 (order 18.10.2026): cancels this direction's pending one-shot fire, because pressing Stop in the GUI means "stop, and do not come back on your own".
Measured on 18.10.2026: Stop only cancelled the RUNNING cycle (_stopCts) and wrote a marker; the armed fire was untouched and nothing in the fire path reads that marker, so a deferred upload re-armed itself and started as if the operator had not pressed anything. The marker was not even a backstop: both pipelines clear the markers at run start, so the fire wiped its own stop signal.
The slot's reschedule counter is reset as well: the fire was removed by the operator, not exhausted by the 16x budget, so the next genuine deferral gets its full allowance.
member.returns: True when a fire was pending and is now gone.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSchedulerCoordinator.ScheduleScanDeferFire(System.Boolean,System.DateTime,System.Int32)
member.summary:
F-M475: arms the retry a library-scan deferral needs — exactly now + JobSpacingMinutes, no jitter, on the direction that was deferred.
Replaces the in-process timer the scan deferral used until now. That timer re-ran the ARRIVAL cycle (TimerFiredAsync), so with no arrivals it did nothing at all (measured 15.11.2026: deferred 03:38:10, timer fired 03:53:10, cycle start "event", "no arrivals collected — no run", download task still on its 03:38 run), it was invisible to the status line (which reads pending fires), and it died with the process.
The SOONER attempt wins: a pending quota fire may sit hours in the future while the scan it waited for is already gone, so an earlier scan retry replaces it. A fire that is already earlier than the new one is kept — nothing is pushed back.
member.param: The moment (UTC) the deferred direction may try again.
The spacing that produced the moment — carried into the reason text.
member.returns: True when this call armed the fire; false when an earlier one was already pending.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSchedulerCoordinator.GetPendingFires
member.summary:
Every pending one-shot fire, keyed by the WORKER it belongs to (F-M294, user decision 03.10.2026: "defer whenever a fire was scheduled, whichever worker").
The GUI needs this to paint a worker's lamp yellow and to name the moment. Only DEFERRED re-fires appear here — the regular anchors are computed from the interval and carry no stored fire, so a worker that is simply waiting for its next window is not "deferred".
The seeder has no fire of its own: it runs inside a cycle, driven by whichever direction triggered it. The five keys below are exactly the workers that can hold one.
member.returns: Worker key → the moment (UTC) that worker's fire is due. Empty when nothing is pending.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSchedulerCoordinator.ClearStaleTriggers
member.summary: F-M48: fixed-time triggers are forbidden — all scheduled fires come from the coordinator's random anchors. JF persists dashboard trigger edits as {ConfigurationDirectory}/scheduledtasks/{TaskId}.js; installs that ran an older version (or where the user edited triggers) still carry the old DailyTrigger there. member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSchedulerCoordinator.IsLibraryScanRunning
member.summary: True when the given plugin task type is registered with the TaskManager. During early startup Jellyfin has not registered the plugin's tasks yet, and QueueScheduledTask at that moment logs "Unable to find scheduled task of type ... in QueueScheduledTask" and DROPS the fire silently. Every fire path must therefore test this BEFORE it consumes its marker (or resets its reschedule counter), so an unregistered task leaves the slot claimable and the next 30-s tick retries it. Same guard class as the F-M65 recovery fires, which had it for download/upload only (F-M212).

F-M448: true while Jellyfin is building or validating a library (or refreshing the metadata of freshly imported items). A scan creates the item first and attaches its media streams when its analysis runs — a seed that looks in between finds an item with no stream list at all.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSchedulerCoordinator.PersistSchedulerState
member.summary: (user decision 29.09.2026): mirror the WHOLE scheduler state to scheduler-state.json. Every dedup test in this class is answered against a RAM field, so without this a Jellyfin restart re-claims slots that already fired today and re-runs work that was done: measured on prod 28.09.2026 (OSHash anchor Sunday 07:46) 23 restarts produced 22 OSHash fires against ONE real anchor fire, and postprocessing fired 22 times with 20 of them 0-1 s after a restart. The marker counts the CLAIM, not the outcome — a run that fails after being queued stays consumed for the day, exactly as it did before. Written at most once per tick and only when something actually changed.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSchedulerCoordinator.LoadSchedulerState
member.summary: (user decision 29.09.2026): reload the scheduler state on startup. A marker restored from disk is already consumed for its day, so the due-test skips the slot until the next anchor day — which is what stops a restart from replaying it. A missing or unreadable file simply leaves the fields at their defaults (the pre-persist behaviour), so a fresh install or a deleted file is never worse.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSeeder.OpenPairsOf(MediaBrowser.Controller.Entities.BaseItem,System.String,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.String},System.Boolean)
member.summary:
F-M282 (user decision 02.10.2026): the subtitle DATA missing for this file, at the grain of the datum.
This replaces the language-keyed MissingLanguagesOf, and with it the fourth copy of the sidecar-name parse (F-M239: a copy without the sdh marker read Movie.de.sdh.srt as the phantom language "SD", so a file carrying its only German variant looked like it was missing German and was queued on every scan) and the MissingHearingImpaired projection that followed it.
That projection is where the model broke: it answered with LANGUAGES whose variant was absent, and the caller dropped those into the same list that drives the search — so a missing variant made the REGULAR subtitle due, and it was fetched over the file already on disk (41 downloads in one run against a 50/day limit, the same content hash on three consecutive days). A pair list cannot be re-projected like that: the regular German and the German variant come back as two entries, and the search asks SubDL for whichever one is actually absent.
The queue gate and the pipeline now ask the SAME reader (), so an item the seeder queues is an item the pipeline has work for — the mismatch that queued 290 items and let the pipeline skip 280 of them as "nothing missing" cannot recur.
member.param: True when embedded streams count as evidence.
member.returns: The pairs without evidence.

Jellyfin item the file belongs to.
member.summary: F-M261 with F-M311: resolves untagged tracks and writes the found languages back, returning how many codes were actually WRITTEN (0 when the switch is off, when the detector could not decide, or in a dry run — the write half stands down there). The return value is what the statistics row counts; the method's own reporting stays as it was.
member.returns: 1 when this file was written, 0 when nothing was written. One per FILE, not per code: the statistics line answers "how many media files did the run edit".

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSeeder.ObserveEmbeddedFacts(MediaBrowser.Controller.Entities.BaseItem,System.String)
member.summary:
F-M257: writes the embedded tracks of this file into the registry as OBSERVATIONS.
This is the write path the embedded area never had. It runs for every scanned item in both directions and regardless of UploadEnabled, because the facts are the file's, not a work decision: which language sits at which position, and whether that track is hearing-impaired. Readers (the HI question, F-M254) can then answer from the registry on an install where the uploader never runs.
Positions are computed against the UNFILTERED subtitle list, exactly like the upload pipeline does: ffmpeg's 0:s:N counts bitmap and forced tracks too, so an index taken from a filtered list would point at a different stream. Forced tracks are skipped for the same reason the pipeline skips them (F-M246) — a forced track carries a handful of cues for foreign-language scenes and is not a subtitle of the film.
Failure is swallowed on purpose: an observation is an improvement, never a precondition. A scan that cannot read the streams must still queue its items normally.
member.returns: Number of rows created or changed.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSeeder.DryRunActive
member.summary: F-M312: true when EITHER direction has a dry run armed, so the write halves must stand down. One predicate for the whole seeder, mirroring LanguageTagGate.DryRunActive — the seeder belongs to no direction (it scans before both), so tying a write to one switch would let the other dry run edit the library, which is exactly what F-M22 forbids.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSeeder.RenameSidecar(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Boolean,System.Boolean@)
member.summary:
Moves an unlabelled sidecar onto the name this plugin writes, once its language is known.
F-M278 (user decision 01.10.2026). Only ever called for a file whose name carried NO language token — a file that already names its language is left alone, which is what the caller's wasUnlabeled guard enforces.
The move is refused rather than forced when anything is not as expected: the target already exists (another subtitle of that language is there — a rename must not destroy it), the target name cannot be built, or the filesystem rejects the move. Every refusal leaves the file exactly where it was and returns the original path, so the caller records the fact under a name that is really on disk. A rename is a tidying step, never a precondition for recording.
member.param: Media file the sidecar belongs to.
Current path of the unlabelled sidecar.
The language resolved from the file's text.
True when the sidecar name marks a forced track.

F-M313: true when the file was really moved under a new name. False on every refusal (target taken, unlistable directory, filesystem error, dry run) — the caller counts only real moves, so the statistics line cannot claim a rename that did not happen.
member.returns: The path the file is at after this call — the new one, or the original on any refusal.

member.name: M:Jellyfin.Plugin.SubdlScribe.ScheduledTasks.SubdlSeeder.ObserveSidecarFacts(System.String)
member.summary:
F-M259: writes the loose .srt files beside this media into the registry as OBSERVATIONS.
The sidecar area's only writers were the two pipelines, both behind their own switch — so a subtitle file that no plugin run ever touched (another tool wrote it, it predates the registry, or upload is off) had no row. The download side reads the DISK for "is the language there?" but asks the REGISTRY for the HI question (F-M254): for such a file the language looked present and its hearing-impaired variant looked absent, on every run.
The read is the sidecar's content, because content is the sidecar's identity — the same rule the uploader follows, so a row observed here is the row the uploader would find. Failure is swallowed: an observation is an improvement, never a precondition.
member.returns: Number of rows created or changed, and — via — how many loose files were renamed so their name carries the language (F-M313). Two numbers because they are not the same: a file can be renamed while its row already exists (nothing written), and a file can be recorded without any rename (its name was already correct).
